Add the primary SC judgment https://indiankanoon.org/doc/156623410/ beside or instead of the LSI summary; the LSI print URL returns 406 to curl and opens via WebFetch. Same fixes for force:case-sukna d[3]/d[4] and claim money-people:c084 (move the 'influenced and vitiated' attribution to IBTimes). c085 can go to documented with the indiankanoon link. Keep the officers unnamed in labels and text, since they are below the service-chief threshold.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: Union of India (NDA; MeitY under Ashwini Vaishnaw, MHA under Amit Shah, from 7 Jul 2021) allegedly used Pegasus on Indian phones. The allegation dates from the Citizen Lab/Amnesty report of 15 Jun 2020 and the consortium reports of 18 Jul 2021. The SC order of 27 Oct 2021, the bench's reading of the panel report on 25 Aug 2022 and the 29 Apr 2025 hearing all fall inside the NDA window, so the dates overlap. One slip: the file (c087, from: 2021-07-18) dates the Minister's statement to Parliament as 18 Jul 2021 because the SC order says '18th July 2021'. The suo motu statement was made in the Lok Sabha on 19 Jul 2021, about the media reports of 18 Jul (PIB PRID 1736803, titled '...as reported in Media on 18th July 2021').
verdicts.identityTest: The actor is 'the Government', meaning the Union of India as respondent in WP(Crl) 314/2021 (Manohar Lal Sharma v UoI and connected petitions). The order names the Additional Secretary, MeitY, as the deponent of the 16 Aug 2021 'limited affidavit'. NSO Group is identified as Pegasus's producer in the order. No state government or agency (IB, NTRO, R&AW) is named as user in any source, and the narrative correctly names none. The identity holds at the level of 'Union of India'. It does not hold at the level of any agency.
verdicts.baseRate: Citizen Lab (2018) traced Pegasus operators to about 45 countries, and the 2021 leaked list covered more than 10 countries. India is one of several democracies (Mexico, Hungary, Poland, Spain) where government use is alleged. So 'alleged state Pegasus user' does not single India out. The narrative does not claim it does. It claims only that the question is contested, and that framing does not depend on the base rate.
verdicts.denialFound: Union: the SG reiterated the Minister's statement that unauthorised surveillance does not take place, filed only a limited affidavit and cited national security (SC order, https://indiankanoon.org/doc/39021018/: 'He reiterated the statement dated 18th July 2021 made by the Hon'ble Minister ... which ensures that unauthorized surveillance does not take place'). The narrative leaves out three more denials. (1) MoS Defence Ajay Bhatt told the Rajya Sabha in writing on 9 Aug 2021 that the 'Ministry of Defence has not had any transaction with NSO Group Technologies' (https://scroll.in/latest/1002445/pegasus-row-defence-ministry-has-not-had-any-transaction-with-nso-group-says-centre). (2) After the NYT report of 28 Jan 2022, MoS V K Singh called the NYT 'Supari Media' (https://theprint.in/india/union-minister-v-k-singh-calls-nyt-supari-media-over-its-report-on-pegasus/816036/). (3) The MEA said the matter was before the SC committee and it had 'no information' (https://www.deccanherald.com/india/no-information-available-with-us-mea-on-pegasus-row-1077829.html). None of these is a sworn denial of use by the Union as a whole. MoD's denial covers MoD only.
verdicts.innocentReading: Several readings fit the evidence. Pegasus traces on Indian phones (Amnesty 2021; Amnesty/Washington Post Dec 2023) could come from a foreign government client of NSO. The 5 infected phones the committee found carried malware other than Pegasus. The Union's refusal to file a detailed affidavit could reflect a standard national-security posture that is not specific to Pegasus. Lawful interception under s.5(2) Telegraph Act/s.69 IT Act exists and does not need Pegasus. None of this is excluded, so 'contested' is the right status. 'Documented' would be too high and 'unsupported' too low.
verdicts.reason: All three cited sources say what the narrative attributes to them. The SC order quotes the 'limited affidavit', the 'free pass' line and the SG's reliance on the Minister's statement. The Tribune quotes CJI Ramana: 'In five phones some malware was found but the technical committee says it can't be said to be Pegasus', and reports that the bench quoted the panel as saying the Government did not help it. LawBeat quotes 'To have spyware, there is nothing wrong. The question is against whom it is being used' and 'we are not going to disclose a single word'. 'Contested' is an accurate status for 'the Government used Pegasus'. No court, audit or official record establishes use or non-use, the report is sealed, and the Union has neither confirmed nor specifically denied use on affidavit. The narrative makes no factual assertion beyond that status, names no one below public rank and contains no operational detail. So it is not killed and not refuted. It is incomplete on both sides, though: the strongest case leaves out the NYT purchase report and the Amnesty forensics, and the strongest counter leaves out the MoD Rajya Sabha answer and the MEA statement. The underlying claim stays 'alleged' with its contra, and the narrative stays 'contested'.
verdicts.corrections: 1. strongestCase: add the NYT report of 28 Jan 2022 that India bought Pegasus in 2017 as part of a roughly $2bn India-Israel package. It has one outlet with named sourcing, so tier it 'reported', and attach its denial. Add Amnesty Security Lab's forensic confirmation of Pegasus on Indian journalists' phones (July 2021, and 28 Dec 2023: Varadarajan and Mangnale, last infection Oct 2023, https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2023/12/india-damning-new-forensic-investigation-reveals-repeated-use-of-pegasus-spyware-to-target-high-profile-journalists/). This shows Pegasus was used against Indian citizens but does not attribute it to the Indian state. 2. strongestCounter: add the MoD written answer in the Rajya Sabha of 9 Aug 2021, 'not had any transaction with NSO Group Technologies', which is a documented Parliament answer limited to MoD. Add the MEA 'no information' statement and V K Singh's response to the NYT. 3. c087 'from': change 2021-07-18 to 2021-07-19, the date of the Lok Sabha suo motu statement (PIB PRID 1736803), and note that the SC order calls it 'statement dated 18th July 2021'. 4. Add the PIB statement as a primary source for the Minister's position. Vaishnaw's statement denies 'illegal surveillance' rather than use of Pegasus as such, and the narrative should say so explicitly. 5. whatWouldChangeThis: add 'a sworn affidavit by the Union confirming or denying procurement or use, or disclosure of procurement records'.

verdicts.dateTest: Restated, the claim is: governments of the UPA (2004-14) or NDA (1998-2004, 2014-) <presided over worse> defence scandals <in those windows>. The record makes no directional assertion. Its status is 'speculative'. Its strongestCase is a count of 4 UPA, 2 NDA and 1 earlier, and that count uses a mixed criterion ('decided OR surfaced'), which flatters whichever bucket it is applied to. AgustaWestland: the Wikipedia source confirms 'contract to purchase 12 AgustaWestland AW101 helicopters in February 2010', which is UPA. The specification history goes back to the NDA-I years, but the cited page does not cover it. Tatra/BEML: purchases ran from the 1980s through 2012 under several governments, including NDA-I. Only the surfacing (2012) and the bribe-offer allegation (22 Sep 2010) fall under UPA. Bofors: the contract was 1986 under a Congress government (Rajiv Gandhi). The Delhi HC quashed the corruption charges in Feb 2004 under NDA-I, and the 2005 Hinduja order and the 2011 withdrawal came under UPA. Calling it 'earlier' therefore hides a split decided/surfaced record. Adarsh was a Congress-NCP state matter and Sukna was an internal Army matter. Neither is a Union procurement decision. Pegasus (2021, NDA) is a surveillance matter, not a defence procurement scandal. The count's date attribution does not survive per-case testing.
verdicts.identityTest: The cases are the ones the SPEC names (force:case-bofors, case-rafale, case-agustawestland, etc.), so the case identities hold. The actor 'UPA/NDA' is a coalition label and not an office-holder. It cannot be resolved to a decision-maker per case: Adarsh was a state government, Sukna an Army court of inquiry, and Tatra spanned several governments. The comparison unit (a 'scandal') is undefined. It has no stage, amount or investigator field to compare on.
verdicts.baseRate: Non-discriminating. Every government since 1986 has a headline defence-corruption allegation: Bofors (Congress 1986); Tehelka Operation West End, the Kargil coffin case and Barak (NDA-I 2001-06); AgustaWestland and Tatra (UPA-II); Rafale (NDA-II). That is effectively 100% of governments, well above the 80% threshold. Final convictions are near 0% across all of them. The record's own counter says 'Zero final convictions in all seven'. The AW Wikipedia page confirms no Indian conviction. Tatra charges were framed on 2 Aug 2019 and the trial is ongoing, with no verdict found. The seven cases are a brief-selected sample and not a census. The SPEC's UPA-II vs NDA control cannot be run without a CBI/ED defence case list by year, and the record correctly names that as whatWouldChangeThis. Material omission: the only trial-court convictions in a defence-deal corruption case found in this check come from the NDA-I-era Tehelka sting. Jaya Jaitly, Gopal Pacherwal and Maj Gen S.P. Murgai (retd) were convicted and sentenced to 4 years in July 2020 (Tribune, Deccan Chronicle), and Bangaru Laxman was convicted in 2012. Neither conviction is final: Jaitly's is understood to be stayed on appeal, and Laxman's appeal was pending when he died. Leaving these out makes the UPA-heavy count look more lopsided than the record supports.
verdicts.denialFound: Not applicable as one party's denial, because the narrative accuses no single party. Case-level answers are carried on the other narratives: Dassault/MoD/Reliance on Rafale, the 2005 HC order on Bofors, and the Tyagi side on AgustaWestland. No response from Congress or BJP to the comparative framing was recorded. Nobody was asked.
verdicts.innocentReading: Defence procurement is large, lumpy, agent-mediated and slow. Every government inherits contracts signed under earlier ones, and allegations surface years after the decision. The count of scandals per government therefore mostly tracks when a case surfaced and how long it has had to run (older cases are resolved; newer ones are sealed or still in trial). It does not track relative probity. Courts and agencies have not produced final convictions for either side, so neither partisan reading has an adjudicated basis.
verdicts.reason: The record survives because it asserts nothing. It marks itself 'speculative', presents both directions, and names the missing census. It cannot be refuted as a claim, only corrected as framing. Its strongestCase count (4 UPA / 2 NDA / 1 earlier) does not hold up. It is a conjunction of individually true dates that together imply a UPA skew none of the sources states. It mixes 'decided' with 'surfaced'. It assigns multi-government cases (Tatra, Bofors, arguably AgustaWestland) to one side. It counts a state housing case (Adarsh), an internal Army case (Sukna) and a surveillance case (Pegasus) as defence scandals. And it omits NDA-I (Tehelka, coffin, Barak), which is where the only trial-court convictions found in this check sit. The sources are three Wikipedia pages and do not support the count itself. The tier must be analytic (our own comparison), with innocentReading attached, and not documented or reported.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Set tier to 'analytic' and add an innocentReading (the text above). 2) Consider changing status from 'speculative' to 'unsupported'. No comparative metric or census exists either way, and the record admits the sample is the brief's. 3) Rewrite strongestCase. Drop the bare 4/2/1 count, or tabulate each case by decision government and surfacing government separately: Bofors 1986 Congress / 1987, with the HC quash Feb 2004 under NDA-I; Tatra purchases from 1986 across governments, surfaced 2012 under UPA; AgustaWestland contract Feb 2010 UPA, surfaced 2012-13; Rafale IGA 2016 NDA; Adarsh state Congress-NCP; Sukna Army 2008; Pegasus reported 2021. 4) Flag that Pegasus, Adarsh and Sukna are not Union defence-procurement decisions, or move them out of the comparison. 5) Add NDA-I cases to strongestCounter: Tehelka Operation West End (2001), with trial-court convictions of Bangaru Laxman (2012) and Jaya Jaitly/Pacherwal/Murgai (Jul 2020, 4 yrs; not final). Sources: https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/nation/tehelka-expose-jaya-jaitly-2-others-convicted-in-corruption-case-117863 and https://www.deccanchronicle.com/nation/current-affairs/300720/tehalka-expose-jaya-jaitly-two-others-sentenced-to-4-years-in-jail-f.html. Edit 'Zero final convictions in all seven' to add that trial-court convictions exist outside the sample, in an NDA-I-era sting case. 6) Replace or supplement the Wikipedia-only srcs with the case-level primary records already in narratives 2-5 (Indian Kanoon orders, CAG Report 3 of 2019). 7) Add to whatWouldChangeThis: a Parliament answer listing CBI defence-procurement FIRs and MoD debarments by year and stage, run across NDA-I, UPA-I, UPA-II and NDA-II.

verdicts.dateTest: Restated: "Critics (veterans quoted by The Tribune, 27/28 Jul 2024; Congress President Kharge, letter of 26 Feb 2024) predict that Agnipath, approved 14 Jun 2022, will erode skill and cohesion. The Army (Standing Committee oral evidence, Report 8, Mar 2025) says it is progressing." Every dated item comes after the scheme's approval, and the PIB release shows "Posted On: 14 JUN 2022". There are two problems. (1) The "about 11% of Army JCO/OR strength by Mar 2025" figure pairs two dates. The numerator, "Currently, 1,23,000 Agniveers are enrolled", is from oral evidence given around Feb-Mar 2025. The denominator, held strength of 11,05,110, is "as on 01 October, 2024". The ratio is our own derivation and the report never states it. (2) The file's asOf is 2026-10-04, but strongestCounter still says "the first exits only begin in 2026-27, so no outcome data exists". The exit window is now open: Navy and IAF in Oct-Nov 2026, Army in Dec 2026-Jan 2027. The Services have also asked to raise retention to 50% (Army, IAF) and about 75% (Navy). This was reported by the Indian Express on 6 Jul 2026, via SSBCrack on 4 Oct 2026. The DMA is examining the request and nothing has been notified. This is the Services' own signal on skill retention, it postdates the counter text, and the narrative leaves it out.
verdicts.identityTest: Most actors match their sources. The Army representative's words in the Standing Committee report (18 LS, Defence Report 8, p. ~16) are "Agniveer is the most transformative reform of the Government and the Indian Army is progressing on the path to make it successful. Currently, 1,23,000 Agniveers are enrolled in the Agnipath Scheme." The quote is accurate. It is ambiguous whether 1,23,000 counts the Army alone, although an Army witness gave it. The Tribune quotes two named veterans, both public figures: Brig IS Gakhal (retd) and Maj Gen IP Singh (retd). The "66 per cent" projection is put to "veterans" in general. The Kharge letter of "February 26, 2024" with "parallel cadres" is confirmed on inc.in. The one misattribution: strongestCase says "The terms are documented: four years, six-month training, up to 25% retained, no pension (PIB 14 Jun 2022)". PIB PRID 1833747 confirms four years, "up to 25% of each specific batch of Agniveers will be enrolled in regular cadre" and "There shall be no entitlement to gratuity and pensionary benefits". It says nothing about training length. "Six months" comes from The Tribune: "The training of Agniveers is of about six months."
verdicts.baseRate: The property "most enlisted soldiers leave without a service pension" does not set India apart among volunteer militaries. Under the US legacy 20-year cliff, most enlisted personnel left with no annuity, and short-engagement contracts are standard in the UK and elsewhere. It does set Agnipath apart from India's own pre-2022 system, where other ranks served 15-17 years and became pension-eligible. The theme is common in the media: veteran criticism has appeared regularly since Jun 2022, so the narrative singles out no person. The symmetry control does not apply cleanly, because UPA-II had no comparable recruitment scheme. The file's symmetryCheck already records the Congress objection beside the government defence using identical fields, and I found no asymmetry.
verdicts.denialFound: The record holds the Army's position: Standing Committee Report 8 (Mar 2025), https://sansad.in/getFile/lsscommittee/Defence/18_Defence_8.pdf, "the most transformative reform ... progressing on the path to make it successful". Two items are missing. (a) The PM defended the scheme at Dras on Kargil Vijay Diwas, 26 Jul 2024. The cited Tribune piece frames itself around that defence ("Even as Prime Minister Narendra Modi's remarks on Kargil Vijay Diwas at Dras, defending the Agn[ipath]..."). (b) MoS Home Nityanand Rai told the Rajya Sabha (Aug 2026) that 75% of the first batch are expected to leave, which confirms the terms are unchanged. This platform asked no one. MoD has published no rebuttal on training or cohesion specifically.
verdicts.innocentReading: The scheme is a deliberate trade: a younger age profile and a lower long-run pension liability in exchange for shorter individual service. Peer volunteer armies run similar models without being "hollowed out". The Agniveer share has to rise from zero until the first exits, so a rising share is mechanical and not a sign of erosion. Skill loss can be met by changing the retention ceiling. The Services are already asking for this (50-75%), and the 25% ceiling is "up to" and changeable by notification. No outcome data on cohesion or capability exists yet. So the "hollowing" thesis is a forecast, not a finding.
verdicts.reason: The narrative is not refuted. It is a forecast labelled "contested", it gives both the critics' case and the Army's response, it implies no wrongdoing, and it names only public figures. I opened all four sources and they support the quoted material: PIB on the four-year term, the 25% ceiling and no pension; The Tribune on "seven to eight years" and "66 per cent"; inc.in on "parallel cadres"; and Committee Report 8 on the "most transformative reform" quote and the 1,23,000 figure. Three defects need fixing. (1) "Six-month training" is attributed to PIB, which does not say it; the source is The Tribune. (2) The "about 11%" figure is our own ratio of 1,23,000 to 11,05,110 across mismatched dates (oral evidence around Mar 2025 against held strength on 1 Oct 2024), but it is presented as if the source stated it. (3) As of 2026-10-04 the narrative is stale. It omits the Services' own proposals to raise retention to 50-75%, now under DMA examination and not notified, which is the most probative evidence on the skill question from the party itself. It also says exits "only begin" when the exit window has already opened. "Contested" remains the right status, and analytic is the right tier for the forecast. The underlying terms are documented.
verdicts.corrections:
1. strongestCase: change "The terms are documented: four years, six-month training, up to 25% retained, no pension (PIB 14 Jun 2022)" to "The terms are documented: four years, up to 25% of each batch retained, 'no entitlement to gratuity and pensionary benefits' (PIB 14 Jun 2022); training is about six months (The Tribune, 28 Jul 2024, citing veterans)".
2. strongestCase: change "Agniveers were already about 11% of Army JCO/OR strength by Mar 2025" to "1,23,000 Agniveers enrolled (Army witness, oral evidence, Report 8, Mar 2025) against 11,05,110 JCO/OR held on 1 Oct 2024, about 11% on our arithmetic (dates differ; the report does not state the ratio)".
3. strongestCase or whatWouldChangeThis: add "The Services have themselves proposed raising retention to about 50% (Army, IAF) and about 75% (Navy); the DMA is examining this and no amendment had been notified as of Oct 2026 (Indian Express, 6 Jul 2026, via SSBCrack 4 Oct 2026, https://www.ssbcrack.com/2026/10/first-agniveer-batch-begin-exit-as-armed-forces-seek-higher-permanent-retention.html)". Open the Indian Express original before citing it as primary.
4. strongestCounter: change "the first exits only begin in 2026-27" to "the first exits began in Oct-Nov 2026 (Navy, IAF), with the Army in Dec 2026-Jan 2027; no outcome data has been released". Add the PM's defence of the scheme at Dras on 26 Jul 2024 (referenced in the Tribune source).
5. In the claim text, label the "two-thirds in 10-12 years" figure as "veterans' projection assuming intake rises to 1.75 lakh a year (Tribune)".
6. Add the base-rate note: short service with no pension is normal in volunteer armies and is a change only relative to India's pre-2022 system.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim restated: Union Government (MoD, Demand No. 20) spent ₹7,460 cr on the Agnipath sub-heads in FY2024-25 (actual) and budgets ₹17,396 cr for FY2026-27 (BE); there is no official costed pension saving. The scheme has been in force since Cabinet approval on 14 Jun 2022, so the tenure overlaps: both FYs fall inside it. Column headers in sbe20.pdf (Notes on Demands for Grants 2026-27, p.74) read "Actual 2024-2025 | Budget 2025-2026 | Revised 2025-2026 | Budget 2026-2027", so the FY and stage labels are right. Timing problem in strongestCounter: it says pension savings accrue "from the 2040s". Under the old terms, a 2022 recruit doing the 17-year colour service (the baseline both The Wire and DMA use) would have started drawing pension around 2039. The PM himself framed it as "pension costs that would arise after 30 years". "Late 2030s onward" is closer than "from the 2040s".
verdicts.identityTest: The entity is right. Demand No. 20 Defence Services (Revenue) has three sub-heads named "Agnipath Scheme": 1.12 Army (6216.74 actual 2024-25, 15173.68 BE 2026-27), 2.08 Navy (544.65, 1150.50) and 3.06 Air Force (698.36, 1072.00). They sum to 7,459.75 and 17,396.18, which round to ₹7,460 cr and ₹17,396 cr. The unit is ₹ crore, as the PDF header states. The 8th CPC ToR (PIB PRID 2183289) does contain "iii. The unfunded cost of non-contributory pension schemes". PIB PRID 1833747 does say "There shall be no entitlement to gratuity and pensionary benefits" and "up to 25% of each specific batch". Its "46,000 Agniveers to be recruited this year" refers to 2022 only. The strongestCase's "each 46,000-a-year intake" turns that one-year figure into an annual one.
verdicts.baseRate: Not a discriminating-property claim. The symmetry test is whether every no-pension or contributory-pension reform gets the same reading. The 2004 move of civil Central Government employees to NPS (introduced under NDA-I and kept by UPA-I/II) is also routinely described as "saving pension" with no published official costed saving, and its fiscal gain also arrives decades later. The same lens gives the same reading on the control, so it is not partisan. In practice no Indian pension reform comes with a published actuarial with/without projection. Agnipath having no costed saving is therefore the norm, not something that marks this scheme out.
verdicts.denialFound:
Yes, and the record leaves it out.
(1) PM Modi at Drass on Kargil Vijay Diwas, 26 Jul 2024: some people were spreading the misconception that the scheme was meant to save pension money, and he asked why the government would decide today to save pension costs that would arise after 30 years (Business Standard, https://www.business-standard.com/politics/on-kargil-vijay-diwas-pm-slams-oppn-for-playing-politics-over-agnipath-124072601235_1.html; Tribune, https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/j-k/agnipath-crucial-reform-will-keep-forces-battle-ready-pm-643587/amp).
(2) Rajnath Singh, Jun 2022: saving on pensions was the "last thing on the government's mind" (as quoted in The Wire, 21 Jun 2022, https://thewire.in/security/agnipath-scheme-pension-savings-military-denial).
(3) Lt Gen Anil Puri (DMA), Jun 2022: pension savings not a consideration (cited in research/raw/force/AUDIT.json line 1650).
On the other side, The Wire, 21 Jun 2022, reports: "Initially, however, the DMA had estimated that the saving on a solitary Agniveer who served out his full four-year term, instead of the standard 17-year 'colour service' ... would total to around Rs 11.5 crore." Congress called the PM's 2024 remark a "blatant lie".
verdicts.innocentReading: The ₹7,460 cr / ₹17,396 cr Agnipath lines are mostly money that would have been spent anyway. Agniveers replaced regular sepoy, sailor and airman intake, so their pay and the Government's matching corpus contribution would otherwise sit inside "Pay and Allowances" for regular recruits. The rise from ₹7,460 cr to ₹17,396 cr comes from more cohorts being on the rolls, not from new cost. Calling the line "a present cost" of the scheme overstates the net cost, just as "Agnipath saves ₹X crore" overstates a saving nobody has costed. The boring reading: the scheme moves spending from future pensions to present pay plus a one-time Seva Nidhi (which is matched by government corpus contributions). The net effect is unknown without an actuarial projection, which is what the "speculative" status already says.
verdicts.reason:
The figures hold up exactly. sbe20.pdf sub-heads 1.12, 2.08 and 3.06 sum to 7,459.75 (Actual 2024-25) and 17,396.18 (BE 2026-27), and the PIB and 8th CPC ToR quotes match. "Speculative" is the right status: no published official aggregate saving exists, and the Government denies that pensions were the motive. So the narrative is not refuted. Three things are wrong with it:
(a) "No official costed saving" is too absolute. The Wire reports an internal DMA estimate of about ₹11.5 cr saved per Agniveer. That is reported and unverified against a primary record, but it is an official per-head costing and belongs in strongestCase.
(b) The Government's on-record denial (PM, Drass, 26 Jul 2024; Rajnath Singh, Jun 2022) is the main counter and is missing from strongestCounter.
(c) The "present cost" framing treats a gross line that largely replaces regular-recruit pay as if it were a net added cost.
The record should be repaired, not killed.
