(blank) under Actual 2024-25 and BE 2025-26. The 2025-26 sbe20 has no 'spectrum' line at all (0 hits), so the lines first appear at the revised stage. The record window (2025-04-01 to 2027-03-31) covers both years. The timing also fits the late-June 2025 Cabinet decision on government departments' spectrum dues (Bridge Chronicle, 29 Jun 2025). That decision came after BE 2025-26 and before RE 2025-26, which explains why the line appears at RE. No date conflict.
verdicts.identityTest: The entity is the right one. The PDF header reads 'MINISTRY OF DEFENCE / DEMAND NO. 20 / Defence Services (Revenue)', with amounts '(In ₹ crores)'. Line items: 6.04 Spectrum Charges (Army) RE 17469.13, BE26-27 19769.03; 7.05 (Navy) RE 8661.43, BE 9036.43; 8.04 (Air Force) RE 10000.00, BE 8394.54. All three match. The sums are 36,130.56 and 37,200.00. The Net Grand Total is BE 2025-26 311,732.30 and RE 2025-26 349,770.06, a difference of 38,037.76, which matches. The ₹38,037.76 crore is the net figure; the gross difference is 40,122.96. Note text, quoted: 'Spectrum Charges: (Line Items. 6.04, 7.05, 8.04) This includes payment of current spectrum charges and previous dues of principal and late fee components payable to Department of Telecommunication.' PRS, quoted: 'This is mainly due to additional expenditure of Rs 36,131 crore estimated at the revised stage towards spectrum charges. In 2026-27, Rs 37,200 crore has been allocated towards spectrum charges.' PRS's '8% higher' refers to the whole MoD allocation, not Demand 20 alone. The claim does not join unrelated facts to imply something: it rests on one primary record plus PRS restating it. ORF ('A Spectrum Surprise for India's Defence Budget 2026-27') independently reads the same entry the same way.
verdicts.baseRate: This does not single defence out. The June 2025 Cabinet settlement on spectrum dues (penalties and roughly 95% of interest waived; principal plus 5% interest payable) covered Defence, Railways, Space and I&B/Prasar Bharati, as reported by Bridge Chronicle. Every government department that holds spectrum is in the same position. Booking a fee paid to another department as the paying department's expenditure is standard Union accounting; Railways pays spectrum charges the same way. The party-symmetry control does not apply, because no party wrongdoing is asserted. The record already treats the line as a non-partisan step change next to the 6th and 7th CPC and OROP.
verdicts.denialFound: None found, and MoD was not asked. The claim alleges no wrongdoing, so no denial is required for the analytic tier. The government's own explanation is the budget note quoted above.
verdicts.innocentReading: The arithmetic is accurate, and the record's innocent reading is the boring one. After the 2025 Cabinet decision on government spectrum dues, MoD pays DoT for current spectrum use and a reduced backlog of principal and late fees. This is a transfer between two Union departments that raises the defence revenue total without adding to force strength, so the line should be netted out of growth comparisons. One overstatement: the current-charges part pays for spectrum the forces actually use, so 'without buying any force' is too strong.
verdicts.reason: Both sources say what the claim says. The primary Expenditure Budget document gives the three line items to the paisa, the net RE-BE difference, the newness of the lines (blank in Actual 2024-25 and BE 2025-26, absent from the 2025-26 document) and the DoT payee note. PRS gives the same ₹36,131 crore and ₹37,200 crore and the same reading. Analytic is the right tier: the facts are documented, and 'booked as defence spending / inflates the total' is our own accounting inference, carries an innocentReading and implies no wrongdoing. What survives is the accounting point only; nothing in the claim supports misconduct.
verdicts.corrections: 1) In lab/text, write 'Net RE 2025-26 exceeds net BE by ₹38,037.76 crore'; the gross difference is ₹40,122.96 crore. 2) benefit.who / edge: the money flows from MoD to DoT. Either set t to the DoT node (min:department-of-telecommunications), keeping pred 'analytic', or say in d that the receiving party is DoT. s=t=MoD with benefit.who=MoD wrongly names the payer as the beneficiary. 3) Change benefit.how from 'without buying any force' to 'part of it is arrears and late fees; the current-charges part pays for spectrum the services use'. 4) Add context to d: the June 2025 Cabinet settlement of spectrum dues for Defence, Railways, Space and I&B (penalties and about 95% of interest waived; principal plus 5% interest) explains why the line appears at RE. Mark that context as reported (Bridge Chronicle, https://www.thebridgechronicle.com/tech/union-cabinet-spectrum-dues-waiver-6-lakh-crore-2025) until a PIB or Cabinet release is found. 5) Optionally add ORF (https://www.orfonline.org/research/a-spectrum-surprise-for-india-s-defence-budget-2026-27) as an independent reading: spectrum charges are 70% of the MoD RE 2025-26 increase. 6) PRS's '8% higher' applies to the whole MoD allocation, not Demand 20; do not attribute it to the Demand 20 delta. 7) upgradeIf stands: match the DoT receipt-budget line.

The record's from/to window, 2024-01-01 to 2024-12-31, matches the 2024 column of SIPRI-Milex-data-1949-2025_v1.2.xlsx. No actor tenure is involved. The workbook also has a 2025 column (India 2.30%, China 1.72%, Pakistan 2.91%, US 3.12%, UK 2.35%), so 2024 is not the latest year available. That is acceptable as long as the label says 2024, which it does.
verdicts.identityTest: The node is min:ministry-of-defence, but SIPRI's India series is not just the MoD. Footnote 59 says verbatim: "The figures for India include expenditure on the paramilitary forces of the Border Security Force, the Central Reserve Police Force, the Assam Rifles, the Indo-Tibetan Border Police and, from 2007, the Sashastra Seema Bal but do not include spending on military nuclear activities." Footnote 55 says China's figure is SIPRI's own revised estimate (Tian & Su 2021), not the official budget.
verdicts.baseRate: This is a descriptive peer comparison and makes no discriminating attribution, so base rate does not apply. It is a symmetric lens: the same SIPRI series and year are used for all five countries.
verdicts.denialFound: Not applicable. This is a statistical descriptor with no accusation in it, so no response was sought. None found; not asked.
verdicts.innocentReading: Differences in % of GDP reflect differences in GDP size, threat environment, force structure and accounting coverage, such as paramilitary and pensions being included for India and Pakistan, US NIP intelligence and Ukraine aid in the US figure, and an estimated figure for China. They do not show over- or under-spending on their own.
verdicts.reason: I opened the SIPRI xlsx (v1.2) and every number matches. Share of GDP 2024: India 0.022234, China 0.016640, Pakistan 0.027300, US 0.034299, UK 0.024367. Constant 2024 US$ m: India 85,597, China 311,900 (3.64× India), Pakistan 10,303 (0.120× India). Share of government spending: India 7.63%, China 5.05%, Pakistan 14.02%, US 9.05%, UK 5.60%. Add: "SIPRI's China figure is its own estimate, above the official budget (fn 55)". (3) Field d mentions only India's paramilitary inclusion. Add that Pakistan's series also includes paramilitary forces and pensions (fn 60), and that the US figure includes part of the National Intelligence Program and Ukraine aid (fn 44). verdicts.dateTest: The claim, restated: "The Union, through the Department of Revenue (Ministry of Finance, not the MHA), raised spending on the Enforcement Directorate revenue line from an actual ₹60.57 crore in FY2013-14 to ₹516.09 crore in FY2024-25." The NDA took office on 26 May 2014. FY2013-14, the base year, is the last UPA-II year. BE 2014-15 (₹81.01 cr) comes from the full Budget of July 2014, so it is the NDA's. Every year after the base falls inside the NDA window, so the dates line up. One problem: the "before FY2014-15" counter-rate of 16.2% runs from BE 2004-05 to BE 2013-14. That covers UPA-I and UPA-II, which is not the SPEC control (UPA-II, FY2009-10 to FY2013-14), and it is a BE rate set against an NDA rate built from actuals. Like for like, the rates are: actuals UPA-II 14.4% a year (35.34 to 60.57) against NDA 21.5%; budget estimates 16.2% (2004-05 to 2013-14) against 19.0% (2014-15 to 2025-26). On the SPEC control, BE alone for UPA-II is 8.3% a year (51.42 to 70.86), but BE 2009-10 is an outlier: the actual that year was 35.34. The file's own symmetryCheck already carries 14.4% against 21.5%. The narrative text should use that figure, not the 16.2% BE rate.
verdicts.identityTest: The line is correct: "Enforcement Directorate", Major Head 2047 (Other Fiscal Services), in the Department of Revenue Demand. That is Demand 42 in 2013-14, 43 in 2015-16 and 35 in 2026-27. In both 2013-14 and 2026-27 the line is revenue only. ED capital sits under "Capital Outlay for Other Fiscal Services" and the housing lines, so the series is consistent across years but understates the agency's total spend, and the field should say "ED revenue line". Figures checked against the printed pages, all in ₹ crore. sbe35 2026-27: "2. Enforcement Directorate 516.09 … 550.75 … 606.50 … 594.97" (Actual 2024-25 / BE 2025-26 / RE 2025-26 / BE 2026-27). ub2015-16 sbe43: "5. Enforcement Directorate 2047 ... 60.57 ... 81.01 ... 85.20 ... 107.44" (Actual 2013-14 / BE 2014-15 / RE / BE 2015-16). ub2005-06 sbe42: "4. Enforcement Directorate 2047 ... 18.40" (BE 2004-05). ub2013-14 sbe42: BE 2013-14 70.86. Budget at a Glance 2026-27: "Total Expenditure 4652867" (Actual 2024-25). Against the FY2013-14 total of ₹15,59,447 cr that gives x2.984. The increase of 455.52 is 0.00979% of FY2024-25 expenditure, and 516.09 is 0.0111%. All the arithmetic checks out.
verdicts.baseRate: Per the same file's symmetryCheck, across the Union force and agency lines (UPA-II against NDA, actuals): the seven CAPFs grew 12.4% against 10.1% a year, Delhi Police 11.7% against 10.1%, CBI 3.6% against 7.6%, IB 13.6% against 9.6%, ED 14.4% against 21.5%, and Union total expenditure 11.1% against 10.8%. Three agency lines accelerated: ED, CBI and IB. The forces did not. Faster growth under the NDA is therefore not a near-universal property, and it does discriminate. The ED has both the fastest growth and the largest gap over the Union total. The share of the budget remains negligible at 0.011% of Union expenditure.
verdicts.denialFound: No denial on the budget figure exists, and nobody was asked. The figure is the government's own published line. The agency's position runs the other way. ED Annual Report 2024-25 (https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2025/may/doc202551549501.pdf, p.183) says: "no cadre review of ED has been carried out for the last 14 years … there has been an exponential increase in the number of cases … additional responsibility was entrusted to the Directorate in 2018 to enforce FEOA, 2018 without corresponding augmentation in manpower". It quotes FATF MER 2024 para 251: "there is a need to increase the resourcing of ED." The government's line on how ED's powers are used is the MoS (Pankaj Chaudhary) answer to LS USQ 1310 of 08.12.2025, which gives a conviction rate of 53/56 = 94.64% on merits. That addresses the use of powers, not the budget.
verdicts.innocentReading: The likely explanation is mandate growth plus pay. PMLA's schedule widened in 2009, 2012 and 2019, FEOA came in 2018, and FATF pressure built toward the 2024 mutual evaluation. The 7th CPC (2016) and DA indexation raised pay. The ED was also very small in FY2013-14: ₹60.57 cr against 2,063 sanctioned posts is about ₹2.9 lakh per post, which implies a large vacancy or a below-BE base year (BE 2013-14 was 70.86). Filling posts already sanctioned in 2011, plus office expansion (5 regions, 27 zones, 18 sub-zones, all North-East states), would by itself multiply a revenue line made up mostly of salaries. The same budget lens shows only a modest UPA-II rate (14.4%), so the acceleration is real, but it comes from a tiny base and says nothing about whom the agency targets.
verdicts.reason: Every figure checks out against the primary Notes on Demands and Budget at a Glance: 60.57, 516.09, 81.01, 550.75, 18.40, 70.86, total expenditure 46,52,867, and the ECIR and search counts (LS USQ 1310). The status "contested" and the analytic tier fit the evidence, so the narrative survives. Three framing defects in the counter-case need fixing, but none of them reverses the finding. (1) The headline text sets an NDA actuals rate (21.5%) against a pre-2014 BE rate (16.2%) and skips the SPEC's UPA-II control. Like for like, the actuals are 14.4% against 21.5%, which strengthens rather than weakens the acceleration. (2) "ECIRs moved from under 200 a year to 775 with the budget" says something the data does not. ECIRs stayed flat at 110–187 a year from FY2013-14 to FY2018-19 while the budget rose x3.5 (60.57 to 212.53). They then jumped in FY2019-20 (557), peaked at 1,116 in FY2021-22, and fell to 698 in FY2023-24 while the budget kept rising. The endpoints match, but the timing does not. (3) Citing the 2011 cadre restructuring as pre-NDA groundwork leaves out what the same source says: "Since 2011, there has been no increase in manpower"; sanctioned strength is now 2,030. Posts did not drive the budget growth. The money per sanctioned post did, through vacancy filling, pay commission and operations, and the source gives no working-strength figure to split those apart.
verdicts.corrections: 1) narrative.text: replace "the line grew 16.2% a year in budget estimates before FY2014-15" with like-for-like rates: "UPA-II actuals 14.4% a year (FY2009-10 ₹35.34 cr to FY2013-14 ₹60.57 cr) against NDA 21.5%; in budget estimates 16.2% (BE 2004-05 to BE 2013-14) against 19.0% (BE 2014-15 to BE 2025-26)". 2) narrative.text / strongestCounter: drop "with the budget" / "the workload data move with the budget". Replace with: "ECIRs were flat (110–187 a year) through FY2018-19 while the line rose x3.5, then jumped from FY2019-20 (557; peak 1,116 FY2021-22; 775 FY2024-25)". Source: LS USQ 1310, Annexure I; ED AR 2024-25 p.104. 3) The cadre point: add "sanctioned strength has not risen since 2011 (now 2,030; ED AR 2024-25 p.183), so growth is per post, not from new posts; working strength unreported". 4) Label the series "ED revenue line (MH 2047); ED capital is booked under Capital Outlay for Other Fiscal Services and is excluded". 5) srcs: add the files that carry the quoted figures but are not cited: Expenditure Budget 2015-16 Demand 43 (https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/budget_archive/ub2015-16/eb/sbe43.pdf) for Actual 2013-14 60.57 and BE 2014-15 81.01; Expenditure Budget 2005-06 Demand 42 (https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/budget_archive/ub2005-06/eb/sbe42.pdf) for BE 2004-05 18.40; Budget at a Glance 2026-27 (https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/doc/Budget_at_Glance/bag1.pdf) and 2015-16 for total expenditure 46,52,867 / 15,59,447. 6) Add a contra/innocent-reading line citing ED AR 2024-25 p.183 (no cadre review in 14 years; FATF MER 2024 para 251 calls for more ED resourcing).

verdicts.dateTest: Restated as: Union (MHA) controls and funds the Delhi Police, FY1999-00 to BE FY2026-27, and uses it against the elected Delhi government, with no date given. The control structure dates from Article 239AA (69th Amendment, 1991). It is continuous across every Home Minister, so on the control half nothing fails the date test. The 'used against' half has a date problem. The narrative is written in the present tense ("is ... used against") and paired with BE 2026-27. Since February 2025, however, the Delhi government is BJP-run, the same party as the Union. A present-tense 'used against' at asOf 2026-10-04 therefore has no opposition government for the force to be used against. The friction window is the AAP period: 28 Dec 2013 to 14 Feb 2014 under UPA-II (Home Minister Shinde), then Feb 2015 to Feb 2025 under NDA. The narrative should be scoped to that window.
verdicts.identityTest: Pass. The line is 'Delhi Police', item 5 under Establishment Expenditure in Demand 51 (Police, MHA), Notes on Demands for Grants 2026-27. sbe51.pdf, re-downloaded and read, prints: "5. Delhi Police ... 11881.55 622.10 12503.65" (BE 2026-27 revenue, capital, total, ₹ crore). The Grand Total is 173802.53, so 12503.65/173802.53 = 7.19%, and the narrative's 7.2% is correct. One caveat: the same demand carries a second Delhi Police line, item 14.02 under 'Police Infrastructure' (office and residential buildings), at ₹342.50 cr BE 2026-27. That line is not in the ₹12,503.65 cr. Article 239AA(3)(a) is confirmed in the Indian Kanoon text of GNCTD v UoI (11 May 2023), which excepts "Entries 1, 2 and 18 of the State List". The 2023 judgment also quotes the 2018 majority's para 284.16: "the Union of India has exclusive executive power with respect to NCT of Delhi relating to the three matters in the State List in respect of which the power of the Delhi Legislative Assembly has been excluded". Paras 159-160 likewise refer to "the limitation laid down in Article 239AA(3)(a) on NCTD's legislative and executive power by excluding matters related to 'public order', 'police', and 'land'". The claim that the 2023 Court quoted the 2018 Bench on executive power is accurate.
verdicts.baseRate:
Growth, recomputed from the actuals in the file:
- UPA-II, FY09-10 to FY13-14: Delhi Police 11.73% a year against 11.90% for the Police demand.
- NDA, FY13-14 base to FY24-25: Delhi Police 10.14% against 10.30%.
- On the headline totals, "no faster than the Police demand" holds in both periods.

The NDA comparison has a composition problem. J&K Police (₹8,553.38 cr actual 2024-25) entered the Police demand only after the 2019 reorganisation, and NIA and NCB (in Demand 55 in 2013-14) later moved out. Like for like, the rest of the Police demand grew about 9.73% a year under NDA, so Delhi Police grew slightly faster (10.14%). The gap is about 0.4 percentage points either way. That does not discriminate.

Structural comparison: of the UTs with legislatures, police is reserved to the Union in Delhi (Article 239AA) and in J&K (Reorganisation Act 2019). Union control of a capital's police is the stated rationale. The 'used against' half has no base rate in the file: no cases, FIRs or outcomes for any government.
verdicts.denialFound: Not in the file. The accusing side exists as a named party: AAP spokesperson Saurabh Bhardwaj called the Delhi Police the "armed wing of BJP" (Outlook, https://www.outlookindia.com/national/india-news-aap-calls-delhi-police-armed-wing-of-bjp-blames-home-minister-amit-shah-for-citys-failing-law-order-news-341743), and the Delhi government accused the Modi government of using the force against AAP MLAs. A search found no formal denial from the Delhi Police or the MHA. They were not asked for this file. Their response is a gap, not a neutral fact.
verdicts.innocentReading: Delhi is the seat of the Union government, Parliament, embassies and the Supreme Court. Parliament reserved police and public order to the Union in 1991, and the 2018 and 2023 Constitution Benches upheld this. The Delhi Police budget tracks pay commissions and headcount at roughly the rate of the other Police-demand lines. Conflict between the Union and Delhi over the force is structural, not tied to one party. In January 2014 Kejriwal held a sit-in (dharna) demanding control of the Delhi Police from the UPA-II Home Ministry under Shinde. Since February 2025, with BJP in power in both, the friction has no partisan axis.
verdicts.reason:
The claim survives because it does not assert the contested half. Every figure checks against the primary sources:
- ₹12,503.65 cr BE 2026-27 in Demand 51.
- 7.19% of the demand's ₹1,73,802.53 cr Grand Total.
- Article 239AA(3)(a)'s exclusion of Entries 1, 2 and 18.
- The 2023 Court quoting the 2018 para 284.16 on the Union's exclusive executive power.
- UPA-II and NDA growth rates that match the file's actuals: 11.7% and 10.1% for Delhi Police against 11.9% and 10.3% for the demand.

The narrative's status is 'contested'. It correctly says the 'used against' half needs court records the file does not hold. That makes it a calibrated analytic node, not an assertion, and analytic is the right tier.

It still needs corrections:
1. "No faster than the Police demand" depends on headline totals inflated by J&K Police joining the demand in 2019. Like for like, Delhi Police grew marginally faster, by about 0.4 percentage points.
2. Present-tense 'used against' is undated even though Delhi has been BJP-run since February 2025.
3. The UPA-II control is mis-specified for the 'used against' half. Delhi was Congress-run under UPA-II except for AAP's 49 days. The discriminating controls are NDA-I (1998-2004, against a Congress Delhi government) and the AAP–UPA-II clash of January 2014.
verdicts.corrections:
1. Text: replace "the budget grew no faster than the Police demand" with "the budget grew roughly in line with the Police demand: 11.7% vs 11.9% a year in UPA-II and 10.1% vs 10.3% under NDA. Excluding J&K Police, which entered the demand after 2019, the rest of the demand grew 9.7% a year, so Delhi Police was about 0.4 points faster."
2. Amount label: call ₹12,503.65 cr the "Delhi Police establishment line (Demand 51, item 5)". Note that item 14.02 Police Infrastructure – Delhi Police (₹342.50 cr BE 2026-27) is separate, giving ₹12,846.15 cr for the two lines together.
3. Date: scope the 'used against' half to the AAP-run periods (28 Dec 2013 to 14 Feb 2014; Feb 2015 to Feb 2025). State that from Feb 2025 the Union and Delhi governments are both BJP-run.
4. Symmetry (whatWouldChangeThis / symmetryCheck): replace "Union–Delhi disputes under UPA-II" with NDA-I (1998-2004, Vajpayee/Advani against Sheila Dikshit's Congress government) and the January 2014 Kejriwal dharna against the UPA-II MHA. Keep J&K UT Police (Reorganisation Act 2019) as the structural comparator.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads as: "The Union (MHA, Demand 51 Police) budgets the seven CAPF lines at Rs 1,16,587.16 cr, of which 2.0% is capital, against Defence Services (Demands 20+21) at Rs 5,84,785.45 cr, of which 37.5% is capital, in BE 2026-27; the Police demand was 2.6-4.0% of Union expenditure in FY2009-10 to FY2024-25." verdicts.identityTest:
The entities match the sources.

- **Demand 51 (Police), BE 2026-27 (sbe51 p.176):** CRPF 38,517.93; NSG 1,422.47; BSF 29,567.64; ITBP 11,324.08; CISF 15,973.85 net (16,828.85 gross less 855.00 recoveries); Assam Rifles 8,796.68; SSB 10,984.51. These sum to 1,16,587.16. Capital is 602.01 + 120.62 + 685.80 + 225.80 + 108.83 + 342.02 + 217.64 = 2,302.72, which is 1.98%. "Total- Central Armed Police Forces" is 1,16,789.30 including Departmental Accounting.
- **Demand 20:** "Net ... 365478.98" for BE 2026-27.
- **Demand 21:** "Grand Total ... 219306.47". Together with Demand 20 this gives 5,84,785.45. Capital is 37.50% of it, and CAPFs are 19.94% of it.
- **PRS DFG 2026-27:** "98% of the total allocation on CAPFs is towards revenue expenditure, and 2% towards capital expenditure". PRS Table 4 sanctioned strengths for six forces sum to 10,26,879, which matches "about 10.3 lakh".

One identity problem is in the claim text, not the record. The compressed claim puts "share of Union expenditure flat in a 2.6-4.0% band" right after the CAPF figures, so it reads as the CAPF share. The band is the whole Police demand's share. The seven CAPF lines alone were 2.13% (UPA-II mean), 2.43% (NDA mean) and 2.18% in BE 2026-27.
verdicts.baseRate: A low capital share is not distinctive for this kind of force. PRS says the CAPF split has been about 98:2 revenue to capital year after year ("continuing historical patterns"). Police forces are almost always mostly pay. On the symmetry lens, run in the file's symmetryCheck, the seven CAPF lines grew 12.4% a year under UPA-II against 10.1% under NDA. The Police demand share averaged 3.05% under UPA-II and 3.30% under NDA. The same lens applied to UPA-II gives the same or a faster CAPF build-up, so the money does not single out the current government. The narrative's strongestCounter leaves this out, and it should include it.
verdicts.denialFound: Not applicable in the usual sense: this is a budget-composition analytic and no party is accused. I found no named source that actually circulates "the CAPFs are being used as a parallel army". Two web searches turned up only explainers and forum threads. Because the narrative names nobody who asserts it, it risks being a strawman. Record that as a void, or cite an outlet or party that makes the claim.
verdicts.innocentReading: The CAPFs are statutory MHA forces whose mandate is border guarding, installation security and internal security. Forces like that are mostly salaries, so a budget about one-fifth the size of the Defence Services, with almost no equipment capital, is what such forces look like. It is not a shadow military establishment. The Police demand's share of Union spending moves within a 1.4-point band, and its low point (FY2020-21) is a pandemic effect on the denominator.
verdicts.reason:
Every figure in the claim matches the primary budget documents to the paisa, and PRS independently confirms the 98:2 revenue-to-capital split. The claim is labelled analytic, carries an innocent reading, explicitly leaves operational use out of scope, and names no person, deployment or vendor, so no refusal is triggered. It is not refuted.

The weak point is the capital comparison, which is not like for like. The 2.0% counts only the machinery, equipment and vehicle capital inside the seven establishment lines. The same Police demand carries further CAPF capital elsewhere:
- 14.01 "Building Projects of CAPFs and Central Police Organisations": Rs 5,040.87 cr capital
- 16 "Modernization Plan IV for CAPFs": Rs 252.18 cr
- 12 "BSF Air Wing": Rs 72.01 cr
- 13.02 Border Infrastructure capital outlay: Rs 5,266.51 cr

Defence Demand 21, by contrast, includes land and capital works. Counted like for like, the CAPF capital share is about 6% (and about 10% if border infrastructure is included). That is still far below 37.5%, so the conclusion holds, but the "2.0%" headline overstates the contrast.

Two lesser issues: the band sentence is attached to the wrong subject in the compressed text, and the narrative has no named source.

Neither government stands out, which is what the claim says. It singles nobody out and implies no wrongdoing.
verdicts.denialFound: Not applicable. There is no accusation, and nobody was asked. This is a neutral budget comparison that makes no allegation against any party.
verdicts.innocentReading: The record's own innocent reading holds. These lines are mostly pay, allowances and rations of forces whose size is set by battalion raisings. Both windows contain a pay-commission step: the 6th Pay Commission arrears in FY2008-10 and the 7th in FY2016-17. The FY2009-10 base being swollen by arrears is a real effect that pushes the UPA-II rate down. Different window lengths and the unassigned FY2014-15 step also move the rates by a few tenths of a point.
verdicts.reason: The record's own killIf is triggered: 'The extracted actuals are shown to be mis-transcribed against the printed Notes.' The FY2009-10 Assam Rifles actual was taken from the revenue sub-head (₹2,320.23 crore) instead of the printed force total (₹2,422.94 crore, EB 2011-12, Demand 54, p.180). That puts the UPA-II base ₹102.71 crore too low. The UPA-II rate becomes x1.59 and 12.3% a year, not x1.60 and 12.4%. The source chain is also wrong. The claim cites EB 2013-14 Dem 55, but that edition prints only 'Actual 2011-2012' and contains neither the FY2009-10 nor the FY2013-14 actuals. The editions that actually hold the figures are not cited: EB 2011-12 Dem 54 (FY2009-10), EB 2015-16 Dem 55 (FY2013-14) and EB 2020-21 Dem 48 (FY2018-19). Both errors are small and can be fixed. The direction and reading survive (UPA-II 12.3% beside NDA 10.1%; first four NDA years 14.1%), so the corrected claim should stay analytic rather than be killed. As written, though, the stated figure and its sourcing are wrong.

verdicts.dateTest: Read as a sentence, the claim says the MHA Police demand, net with all lines included, took 3.05% of Union total expenditure on average in FY2009-10 to FY2013-14 and 3.30% in FY2014-15 to FY2024-25 (actuals). No minister is named, so no tenure has to overlap. One small point on the split: FY2014-15 straddles both governments, since UPA presented the interim budget and NDA the July 2014 budget. symmetryCheck says it attributes FY2014-15 to neither Home Minister, yet the mean puts it in the NDA period. If FY2014-15 (3.38%) is dropped, the NDA mean becomes about 3.29%, so nothing material changes. FY2020-21 numerator and denominator both cover the same pandemic year.
verdicts.identityTest: The entity is right: it is the MHA 'Police' demand as numbered in each year's Notes on Demands for Grants (Demand 54 in FY2009-11, 55 in FY2011-14, 48 in FY2014-19, 50 in FY2019-20, 51 from FY2020-21). I opened the EBs and checked the Net 'Grand Total' actuals: FY2018-19 is 91,693.07 (EB 2020-21 sbe48), FY2019-20 is 1,02,027.49 (EB 2021-22 sbe50), FY2020-21 is 91,610.65 (EB 2022-23 sbe51) and FY2024-25 is 1,46,634.82 (EB 2026-27 sbe51, 'Net 135073.72 11561.10 146634.82'). Each matches the budgets rows. The demand's contents shift over time but it remains the same demand. SPG enters from FY2012-13; BADP, Land Port Authority, RRU, NFSU and Modernisation Plan IV appear in later years; Assistance to UTs drops out. The claim defines the series as 'whole demand as published', so this drift is a caveat, not an identity failure.
verdicts.baseRate: This is a descriptive share with no accusation attached, so there is no comparison set of entities to discriminate against. On the symmetry lens, both governments get the same treatment, and the result does not favour either side. The NDA-period average is higher only because FY2014-15 to FY2019-20 rose from 3.38% to 3.96%, the years of the 7th Pay Commission on a demand that is mostly salaries. From FY2020-21 to FY2023-24 the share ran at 2.61-2.81%, below every UPA-II year (2.80-3.20%). A 0.25-point gap between the two averages, inside a 1.35-point band, does not show a change of priority. I recomputed all 16 years from the file's budget rows and the denominators: UPA-II averages 3.051% (range 2.80-3.20) and NDA 3.303% (range 2.61-3.96). Both match the claim exactly.
verdicts.denialFound: Not applicable. This is our own analytic ratio, it accuses no party, and no contra is required. Nobody was asked and no response was sought.
verdicts.innocentReading: The demand is dominated by salaries. Its share jumps when a Pay Commission is implemented (FY2016-17 onward) and falls back when the Union's total grows faster, which happened in FY2020-21 because of pandemic and food-subsidy spending. Total expenditure includes interest and transfers to states, so the ratio measures scale, not priority. What the demand covers has also changed over time (SPG, BADP, LPAI, the universities). Either government would show the same pattern.
verdicts.reason: The numbers hold. Every figure I opened matches the source: the Police demand Net Grand Total actuals in EB 2020-21, 2021-22, 2022-23 and 2026-27, and the total-expenditure actuals in Budget at a Glance 2011-12, 2015-16, 2016-17 (bag3), 2020-21, 2022-23 and 2026-27 ('total expenditure in the Actuals for FY 2024-25 ... ₹46,52,867 crore'). Recomputing from the 16 sourced pairs gives exactly 3.05%, 3.30% and a range of 2.61-3.96%. The claim draws no inference beyond a ratio and carries an innocentReading, so the analytic tier is correct. The remaining problems are presentation and sourcing on the claim record, not substance.

At present the single range reads as if it covers both. (2) srcs lists only EB 2013-14 sbe55 (which gives the FY2011-12 actual) and EB 2026-27 sbe51 for the numerator. (3) Fix the innocentReading. It calls the FY2020-21 low of 2.61% a pure denominator effect, but the numerator also fell 10.2% (1,02,027.49 to 91,610.65 crore; capital 8,901.98 to 4,934.84 crore). Add: "and the numerator fell 10% (capital outlay nearly halved)". (4) Add to d: the NDA mean is driven by FY2016-17 to FY2019-20 (7th Pay Commission), and FY2020-21 to FY2023-24 were below every UPA-II year. verdicts.dateTest: Claim: MHA (Union) funded the Delhi Police line at 11.7% a year from FY2009-10 to FY2013-14 (UPA-II) and at 10.1% a year from FY2014-15 to FY2024-25 (NDA); actuals rose 39% in FY2021-22. The windows match the SPEC control exactly. No minister is named, so there is no tenure to overlap. I recomputed every endpoint from the printed Notes on Demands. FY2009-10: 2,691.37 (EB 2011-12, sbe54, item 19.01 Total). FY2013-14: 4,193.85 (EB 2015-16, sbe55, item 20.01). FY2014-15: 4,616.95 (EB 2016-17, sbe48, item 36.01). FY2020-21: 8,015.66, with BE 2021-22 8,338.12 and RE 11,136.22 (EB 2022-23, sbe51, line 5). FY2021-22: 11,131.48 (EB 2023-24, sbe51). FY2024-25: 12,133.16 and BE 2026-27: 12,503.65 (EB 2026-27, sbe51). That gives CAGR 11.7% for the first window, 10.1% for the second, and +38.9% for the step. The Police demand Grand Total grew 11.9% and 10.05% over the same windows, so 'level with' holds. Methodological caveat: the transition year FY2013-14 to FY2014-15 (+10.1%) falls in neither window, and the first window is a 4-year CAGR beside a 10-year one.
verdicts.identityTest: The entity matches: 'Delhi Police' is a line in the MHA Police demand (Demand 54/55/48/50/51 as renumbered). There is one small inconsistency. Up to FY2014-15 the series uses sub-head .01 'Delhi Police' (for example 19.01 = 2,691.37) and not 'Total-Delhi Police' (2,704.31 in FY2009-10; 4,210.59 in FY2013-14), which adds the traffic, technology and signal schemes. From FY2016-17 the consolidated line 5 includes those schemes. The effect is under 1% and leaves the CAGR at 11.7%. 'Only city police with a Union demand line' holds in substance. Chandigarh Police is Union-funded through Demand 53, but its running cost is merged into UT administration and its only police row is 'Police Housing and Allied works'. J&K Police (Demand 51 item 6 from 2024-25) covers a UT, not a city. One compositional caveat on 'level with the Police demand': J&K Police (8,553.38 actual in FY2024-25) entered Demand 51 in the last year. Without it, NDA-window demand growth is about 9.4%, so Delhi Police is still within one point.
verdicts.baseRate: Growth comparison: non-discriminating. Delhi Police tracks the Police demand in both windows (11.7 vs 11.9; 10.1 vs 10.05–9.4), and the seven CAPF lines are 12.4% vs 10.1%. Under-UPA-faster-than-NDA is the common pattern across the force lines. The FY2021-22 step is discriminating: from FY2020-21 to FY2021-22 actuals the comparable lines rose CRPF +9.5%, BSF +11.0%, ITBP +13.7%, CISF +6.0%, Assam Rifles +10.0%, SSB +15.7%, IB +9.3%, and the whole Police demand +16.4%. Delhi Police rose +38.9%, the only force line above 16%. The higher level persisted (FY2022-23 11,527.29; FY2023-24 12,114.70), so it was not a one-year arrears blip.
verdicts.denialFound: none found — not asked. This is an analytic comparison, and no accusation is made that would call for a response. PRS DFG 2022-23 analysis (https://prsindia.org/budgets/parliament/demand-for-grants-2022-23-analysis-home-affairs) records 'Rs 11,136 crore (2021-22 RE)' but gives no reason. No Standing Committee or Parliament-answer explanation was located.
verdicts.innocentReading: Delhi Police is the capital's police under Article 239AA, and the Union pays for it whoever governs Delhi. Its multi-year growth matches the Police demand under both governments. The FY2021-22 step is not opaque at head level. MHA's Detailed Demands put most of it in one object head, 2055.00.119.01.01.28 'Professional Services', which was 172.20 cr actual in FY2020-21 against a BE of 252.00 cr. It then reached 2,132.05 cr at RE 2021-22 and 2,152.16 cr actual 2021-22, then 1,572.00 cr at RE 2022-23. That accounts for about 1,980 cr (64%) of the 3,116 cr step. Salaries add about 534 cr (6,179.93 to 6,713.98). Boring fits that remain open: outsourced or contract services (manpower, CCTV/communications O&M, IT), a reclassification of payments previously booked elsewhere, or settlement of dues. The Detailed Demands name the head but not the purpose.
verdicts.reason: Every figure, both CAGRs and the +39% step check out against the printed Notes on Demands. The UPA-II/NDA comparison is an honest symmetry control that shows nothing discriminating, and the claim says so through its innocentReading. So it survives as analytic. The part that does not survive as worded is 'unexplained'. MHA's own Detailed Demands for Grants Vol I put about 64% of the step in object head 01.01.28 'Professional Services' (2022-23 edition: https://www.mha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2022-08/DDG_Vol_1_10022022%5B1%5D.pdf; 2023-24 edition: https://www.mha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2023-02/DDGVol1_09022023.pdf). Only the purpose of that ~12x jump is unstated, so 'unexplained' must narrow to 'attributed to Professional Services, purpose unstated'. That partly meets the claim's own upgradeIf. The claim's srcs list also omits the documents that carry four of its endpoint figures. Tier stays analytic. No person below public rank, no unpublished city budget and no operational detail is involved, so there is no kill ground.
verdicts.corrections: 1) text: replace 'an unexplained FY2021-22 step (+39% actual)' with 'a FY2021-22 step (+39% actual; about 64% of it in the object head Professional Services, 172 to 2,152 cr; purpose not stated)'. 2) d: after the BE/RE figures, add 'MHA Detailed Demands for Grants put the revision in 2055.00.119.01.01.28 Professional Services: actual FY2020-21 172.20 cr, BE 2021-22 252.00 cr, RE 2021-22 2,132.05 cr, actual 2021-22 2,152.16 cr, RE 2022-23 1,572.00 cr. Salaries 6,179.93 to 6,713.98 cr.' Remove 'the Notes' description of the line does not state the reason' or keep it and add that the Detailed Demands identify the head but not the purpose. 3) innocentReading: replace 'not explained in the extracted lines, which is a gap' with 'concentrated in Professional Services per the Detailed Demands; the purpose of that head's ~12x rise is the remaining gap'. 4) upgradeIf: narrow to 'A Parliament answer, Standing Committee report or MHA outcome document states what the FY2021-22 Professional Services provision (about 2,132 cr RE) paid for.' Keep killIf, and add 'or Professional Services is shown to absorb a head previously booked under another demand'. 5) srcs: add EB 2011-12 sbe54 (FY2009-10 actual), EB 2015-16 sbe55 (FY2013-14 actual), EB 2016-17 sbe48 (FY2014-15 actual) and EB 2023-24 sbe51 (FY2021-22 actual), plus MHA DDG Vol I 2022-23 and 2023-24 (URLs above). 6) d: note that pre-FY2015-16 figures are sub-head .01 'Delhi Police' rather than 'Total-Delhi Police' (2,704.31 / 4,210.59), a difference under 1%. Also note that the Police demand's FY2024-25 total includes J&K Police (8,553.38), which ex-J&K puts NDA demand growth at about 9.4%.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim, in the actor-did-thing-when form: the Union (MHA, Demand 'Police') provided the IB line ₹874.05 cr in FY2011-12 actual, ₹1,050.20 cr in FY2013-14 actual, ₹1,122.97 cr in FY2014-15 actual, ₹4,013.19 cr in FY2024-25 actual, and ₹6,782.43 cr at BE 2026-27 (capital ₹2,549.54 cr against RE 2025-26 capital ₹257.01 cr). The windows match the SPEC control: UPA-II from FY2009-10 to FY2013-14 and NDA from FY2014-15 on. FY2014-15 is a straddle year. The interim budget was UPA's and the full budget (July 2014) was NDA's, and the claim gives that year to NDA. The step from FY2013-14 to FY2014-15 (+6.9%) is left out of both windows. If the NDA window starts at the last UPA actual (FY2013-14 to FY2024-25, 11 years), the rate is about 13.0% rather than 13.6%, so the gap still holds. The UPA-II window is only two years, which the claim discloses. The pre-FY2011-12 exclusion is correct. The 2012-13 and 2011-12 MHA-demand files show the IB line in Demand 52 with nothing in the BE 2011-12 column, and the IB line appears in the Police demand from FY2011-12, with the Bureau of Immigration as its own line (₹104.85 cr actual).
verdicts.identityTest: The entity matches. 2013-14 sbe55 (Demand 55 Police), line 11, 'Intelligence Bureau': Total 874.05 (Actual 2011-12), made up of 857.14 (2055) and 16.91 (4055). 2015-16 sbe55 line 11: Total 1050.20 (Actual 2013-14). 2016-17 sbe48 (Demand 48 Police) line 27: Total 1122.97 (Actual 2014-15). 2026-27 sbe51 (Demand 51 Police) line 2, 'Intelligence Bureau': 3707.12 / 306.07 / 4013.19 (Actual 2024-25); RE 2025-26 3902.10 / 257.01 / 4159.11; BE 2026-27 4232.89 / 2549.54 / 6782.43. The Bureau of Immigration sits outside the IB line in every year after 2011: a separate line in 2013-14, 2015-16 and 2016-17, and in 2026-27 it appears among the bodies in note 7 (Central Police Organisations). The killIf is therefore not triggered. IB buildings sit in a separate line (Police Infrastructure 14.01), and that line also rose in BE 2026-27 (3508.22 to 5040.87). So the IB capital step is not buildings money moved across from that line. FY2009-10 actual 878.37 = 824.18 + 18.67 + 35.52, from 2011-12 sbe52 (MHA). The 2004-05 Notes quote is accurate: 'This also includes provision for Bureau of Immigration and Border Check Posts managed by Intelligence Bureau.' The 2026-27 Note on the IB says only: 'This provision is for meeting the administrative expenses of Intelligence Bureau which ensures national security by collecting and analyzing information on internal threats, terrorist activities and potential security risks.' It does not explain the capital, so 'unexplained in the Notes' is correct.
verdicts.baseRate:
The pattern is specific to the IB; it is not shared across comparable lines. Same files, nominal CAGR, UPA-II window (FY12 to FY14) against NDA window (FY15 to FY25):
- Whole Police demand: 39,586.76 to 49,853.88, about 12.2% a year; then 56,254.59 to 146,634.82 (net), about 10.1% a year.
- CRPF: 8,912.40 to 11,124.14, about 11.7%; then about 12,747 to 34,020.58, about 10.3%.
- BSF: 8,159.99 to 10,293.62, about 12.3%; then about 9.5% (FY14 to FY25).

Comparable lines grew faster under UPA-II than under NDA. The IB is the reverse: slower than the demand under UPA-II (9.6%) and faster under NDA (13.6%). Applying the same UPA-II-beside-NDA lens to the CAPF lines gives the opposite reading, which is what makes the IB result informative rather than generic.

Caveat: all figures are nominal. CPI inflation averaged about 9 to 10% in FY12 to FY14 and about 5% in FY15 to FY25, so real IB growth under UPA-II was close to zero and under NDA about 8%. The claim must say 'nominal'.

The BE 2026-27 capital jump (about 9.9 times RE) has no counterpart in the CAPF capital lines, which moved within roughly ±50%.
verdicts.denialFound: None found; not asked. This is an analytic claim that alleges no wrongdoing, so no denial is due. For the capital step, ThePrint (https://theprint.in/defence/10x-budget-beef-up-for-intelligence-bureau-capex-after-pahalgam-red-fort-terror-attacks/2842592/) and The Wire (https://m.thewire.in/article/government/74-increase-in-budget-allocations-for-intelligence-bureau-paramilitary-forces-too-get-more-share) both report the ₹2,549.54 cr figure. Neither carries an MHA or official explanation. ThePrint links it to the Pahalgam (April 2025) and Red Fort (November 2025) attacks in its own framing. The Wire says only that the rise 'would involve spending on infrastructure'. No Parliament answer or Detailed Demand was found.
verdicts.innocentReading: The IB's mandate grew after 2014: counter-terror coordination, cyber work and the Multi Agency Centre. Pay commission awards (7th CPC in FY2016-17) inflate establishment-heavy lines, though the CAPFs got the same awards and grew more slowly. The two-year UPA-II window is too short for a stable CAGR. Higher inflation in FY12 to FY14 squeezed nominal-to-real growth for every line. The 2026-27 capital provision is a one-off, lumpy technology or infrastructure provision, publicly linked by the press to the 2025 Pahalgam and Red Fort attacks. A BE is also not an actual, and IB capital BEs have historically been under-spent (for example, BE 2025-26 capital 230.76 against RE 257.01; BE 2012-13 capital 44.50 against RE 30.85).
verdicts.reason: Every figure checks out against primary Notes on Demands for Grants: 874.05, 1050.20, 1122.97, 4013.19, 6782.43, 2549.54, 257.01, 878.37 and the 2004-05 BoI wording. The arithmetic checks out too: (1050.20/874.05)^(1/2) gives 9.6%, and (4013.19/1122.97)^(1/10) gives 13.6% (×3.57). The BoI exclusion is correct, the killIf is not met, and the Notes indeed give no capital breakdown. The base-rate test favours the claim: the whole Police demand, the CRPF and the BSF all show the reverse pattern (faster under UPA-II), so the IB divergence is real. The claim is a comparison only and does not imply wrongdoing, so the analytic tier is right. It names no person, no operational detail and no unpublished budget. It survives, with source-chain and framing fixes. Three load-bearing figures (1050.20, 1122.97, 878.37) come from files missing from srcs. The rates are nominal but not labelled as such. The result is sensitive to which window FY2014-15 falls in.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads as: the Union budget (Department of Revenue Demand 35, ED; DoPT Demand 74, CBI; MHA Police demand, NIA) spent actuals that grew by the stated factors between FY2013-14 and FY2024-25 (NIA FY2011-12 to FY2014-15). No minister or office-holder is the actor. The symmetryCheck notes that ED and CBI are outside MHA and that no Home Minister is credited with them. Every figure is a stage-'Actual' number printed two years later: FY2013-14 actuals come from the 2015-16 Notes on Demands, FY2024-25 actuals from the 2026-27 Notes. The FY windows are stated correctly. The UPA-II/NDA split (ED x1.71 FY2009-10 to FY2013-14, then x8.52) runs the SPEC control on the same line. The date test passes.
verdicts.identityTest: The entities match the printed heads. 'Enforcement Directorate' is a line under Establishment Expenditure in the Department of Revenue demand: Demand 43 in 2015-16 (head 2047) and Demand 35 in 2026-27. The note says it is 'concerned with the enforcement of the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) and Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA)'. 'Central Bureau of Investigation' is item 2.01 of DoPT Demand 74 (Demand 73 in 2015-16). 'National Investigation Agency' is item 14 of Police Demand 55 in 2013-14 and item 30 of Demand 48 in 2016-17. In the 2017-18 Demand 48 there is no NIA line; the NIA appears only in the description of 'Central Police Organisations'. That confirms the claim that the NIA was folded into that line. Scope differs slightly between lines. The ED line is revenue-only at both ends: ED capital (housing, 'Capital Outlay for Other Fiscal Services') sits on separate lines and is excluded both times. The CBI and NIA figures include capital (head 4055). On revenue only the CBI grows 411.75 to 941.62, x2.29, against x2.24 as stated. This does not change the reading.
verdicts.baseRate: The claim brings its own comparators: Union total expenditure x2.98, CBI x2.24, NIA x2.06, and the UPA-II ED rate (14.4% a year) against the NDA rate (21.5% a year). Among the agency lines in the file, the ED is the outlier, so the property discriminates. The claim correctly does not treat agency budget growth as unusual in itself. The symmetryCheck finds that CBI and IB also accelerated under NDA, while the CAPFs and Delhi Police did not. Small-base effect: the ED's whole FY2024-25 line is 0.0111% of Union expenditure, and the claim states this. One caveat should be disclosed. Most of the growth is a single-year step in FY2022-23, from 306.39 to 495.48 actual (+62%). In that same year the 'Other Expenditure' line (tribunals: SAFEMA ATFP, CESTAT, AA-PMLA) shows nil actual, against RE 58.00 and FY2021-22 actual 45.29, and the Secretariat line came in about 33 below RE. That points to a possible one-year booking shift. The endpoints are not affected: in FY2023-24 and FY2024-25 'Other Expenditure' is printed separately (66.30 and 76.06) and the ED line is still 502.12 and 516.09.
verdicts.denialFound: None found, and none was sought. The claim is analytic and alleges no wrongdoing, so no party response is needed. The Ministry of Finance has not commented on the ED line's growth beyond the printed note on demands.
verdicts.innocentReading: Mandate and workload growth on a very small base. PMLA ECIRs and searches rose sharply. Offices opened in all North-East states. The Fugitive Economic Offenders Act 2018 added work. Pay-commission and establishment expansion, plus a possible FY2022-23 reclassification step, raised the level. The CBI's mandate did not change and its line tracked total expenditure. A faster-growing line does not show how an agency's powers are used, and the record carries this reading.
verdicts.reason: Every number checks out against the primary Union budget documents. ED: 'Enforcement Directorate ... 60.57' (Actual 2013-14, ub2015-16 sbe43) and 'Enforcement Directorate 516.09 ... 516.09' (Actual 2024-25, 2026-27 sbe35); ratio 8.52. CBI: 'Total ... 444.24' (ub2015-16 sbe73) and 'Net ... 996.58' (2026-27 sbe74); ratio 2.24. Union total expenditure: 1,559,447 (BaG 2015-16) and 4,652,867 (BaG 2026-27); ratio 2.98. NIA: 'Total ... 37.58' (ub2013-14 sbe55) and 'Total ... 77.59' (ub2016-17 sbe48); ratio 2.06. RE 2015-16 is 92.59, and no NIA line appears in 2017-18. The unit is ₹ crore as printed and the stage is Actual throughout. The claim is a labelled comparison: it carries an innocentReading, runs the UPA-II/NDA control, implies no wrongdoing and names no person. That is the analytic tier. It is not refuted. The remaining problems are in the citations and one disclosure: the cited srcs are not the documents that print the FY2013-14, FY2009-10 and FY2014-15 actuals, and the FY2022-23 step is not flagged.
verdicts.corrections: 1) srcs: add the documents that actually print the endpoint actuals. These are Expenditure Budget 2015-16 Demand 43 (https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/budget_archive/ub2015-16/eb/sbe43.pdf, ED 60.57) and Demand 73 (https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/budget_archive/ub2015-16/eb/sbe73.pdf, CBI 444.24); 2011-12 Demands 41 and 72 (FY2009-10 actuals 35.34 and 386.21); and 2016-17 Demand 48 (https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/budget_archive/ub2016-17/eb/sbe48.pdf, NIA 77.59 and RE 2015-16 92.59). The 2013-14 sbe42, 2013-14 sbe73 and 2014-15 sbe55 cited now print FY2011-12 and FY2012-13 actuals, not the endpoints. 2) d: state the scope.
