Tier stays analytic.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: the ED (actor) spent ₹60.57 cr actual in FY2013-14 and ₹516.09 cr actual in FY2024-25, against 185 and 775 ECIRs recorded in those years. Both are actuals, which matches the from/to window of 2013-04-01 to 2025-03-31. The search series (46 to 2,317) starts in FY2014-15, not FY2013-14, because LS USQ 1310 has no figures before 2014-15. So the headline's "FY2013-14 to FY2024-25 ... searches x50" uses two different base years. The `d` field discloses this but the one-line text hides it.
verdicts.identityTest: The entity is right: the "Enforcement Directorate" line of the Department of Revenue demand (Demand 43 in 2015-16, Demand 35 in 2026-27). The notes describe it as covering "enforcement of the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) and Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA)". Units are ₹ crore as printed. In 2024-25 the line is revenue only (capital shows "..."), and tribunals and AA-PMLA have their own lines, so the scope looks comparable. One citation is wrong. The cited Expenditure Budget 2013-14, Demand 42 (sbe42.pdf) does not contain ₹60.57 cr. Its columns are Actual 2011-12 = 41.49, BE 2012-13 = 53.80, RE 2012-13 = 48.50 and BE 2013-14 = 70.86. The FY2013-14 actual of 60.57 appears in Expenditure Budget 2015-16, Demand 43 (ub2015-16/eb/sbe43.pdf), row "5. Enforcement Directorate 2047 ... 60.57". The FY2024-25 actual is confirmed in EB 2026-27 sbe35: "2. Enforcement Directorate 516.09". The ECIR counts are confirmed in the ED Annual Report 2024-25 table: "2013-14 185 41", and 775 for 2024-25. They also match LS USQ 1310 Annexure I, which gives 2024-25 = 775 and 2014-15 = 181. LS Annexure II gives searches of 46 (2014-15) and 2,317 (2024-25). Annexure III gives prosecution complaints of 64+4 and 333+124. The chairman's note quotes match the report verbatim: "only 1,883 ... averaging fewer than 200 annually" and "5,113 PMLA investigations initiated – averaging 511 ECIRs annually". The arithmetic holds: 0.327, 0.666, x2.03, x4.19, x50.4.
verdicts.baseRate: Spending per ECIR is mostly driven by which end years are chosen. Using the repo's own ED actuals and the AR/LS ECIR counts: 2012-13 = 0.20 (45.32/224), 2013-14 = 0.33, 2015-16 = 0.80 (87.75/110), 2018-19 = 1.40 (212.53/152), 2021-22 = 0.27 (306.39/1,116), 2024-25 = 0.67. Under UPA-II alone, 2012-13 to 2013-14, it rose 62% in one year. With a 2015-16 base the measure falls by about 17%; with a 2018-19 base it halves. The figures are nominal. CPI rose about x1.75 between FY2013-14 and FY2024-25, and the 7th CPC pay revision applied from 2016. In real terms the rise is about 15%, not a doubling. There is no comparable "cost per case" series for CBI, NIA or DRI in the record, so no cross-agency base rate can be computed.
verdicts.denialFound: None found, and the ED was not asked. None is needed: this is an analytic ratio of two official series and alleges no wrongdoing.
verdicts.innocentReading: Most of the change is nominal inflation plus pay-commission revisions. The rest is the ED's wider mandate: FEMA, FEOA, attachment and restitution (₹15,261 cr restituted in 30 cases in FY2024-25), and a fifty-fold rise in searches, with the denominator counting only new PMLA ECIRs. A ratio that ranges from 0.20 to 1.40 across years is noise around a growing workload, not a trend.
verdicts.reason: Every figure checks out against primary records: EB 2015-16 Demand 43, EB 2026-27 Demand 35, ED Annual Report 2024-25 and LS USQ 1310. The claim is tiered analytic, carries its own caveat and implies no wrongdoing, so it survives. It still needs fixes. The FY2013-14 actual is cited to a budget (EB 2013-14) that contains only BE 2013-14 (₹70.86 cr), not the ₹60.57 cr actual. The headline does not say nominal. The search base year differs from the expenditure and ECIR base year. And "roughly doubled" holds only for this pair of end years; across the series the ratio swings between 0.20 and 1.40.
verdicts.corrections: 1) srcs: replace "Expenditure Budget 2013-14, Demand 42" (https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/budget_archive/ub2013-14/eb/sbe42.pdf) with "Expenditure Budget 2015-16, Demand 43 (Department of Revenue), Notes on Demands for Grants" (https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/budget_archive/ub2015-16/eb/sbe43.pdf). That document carries Actual 2013-14 = ₹60.57 cr. 2) text: write "nominal ED actual expenditure per ECIR" and add "about x1.15 at constant CPI". 3) text: change "searches x50" to "searches x50 (FY2014-15 to FY2024-25; no FY2013-14 figure in LS USQ 1310)". 4) d / innocentReading: add the endpoint sensitivity (2012-13 0.20; 2015-16 0.80; 2018-19 1.40; 2021-22 0.27; 2024-25 0.67) so readers do not take "doubled" as a trend. 5) Note that the 185 ECIRs for FY2013-14 come from the ED Annual Report alone; LS USQ 1310 starts at FY2014-15. 6) Edge t=force:pmla-2002 is acceptable only because the text says FEMA/FEOA spending is not separated; keep that caveat in the label.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim restated: the Union budget (Department of Revenue demand, ED line) set BE 2004-05 at ₹18.40 cr and BE 2013-14 at ₹70.86 cr, against BE 2014-15 ₹81.01 cr and BE 2025-26 ₹550.75 cr. On the windows: the July 2004 budget (UPA-I) was the first to give BE 2004-05. The ub2014-15 edition gives BE 2014-15 (the July 2014 budget, NDA). So 2004-05 to 2013-14 is UPA-I and UPA-II, and 2014-15 to 2025-26 is NDA. The windows line up with who held office. The claim is about agency budgets, not people: the file attributes no ED line to a Home Minister because the ED sits under Finance, which is correct. One windowing quirk: the step from BE 2013-14 to BE 2014-15 (70.86 to 81.01) is left out of both windows. That is fine because the government changed between those two budgets. The windows do differ in length (9 years against 11), and the innocent reading already says so.
verdicts.identityTest: The entity matches. Each Notes on Demands for Grants PDF I downloaded prints line '5. Enforcement Directorate', major head 2047, under the Department of Revenue demand, in '(In crores of Rupees)'. The figures are in crore, not lakh. Demand numbers by edition: Demand 42 in EB 2004-05 and EB 2013-14/2014-15, Demand 43 in EB 2015-16, Demand 35 in EB 2025-26 and EB 2026-27. Edge s=force:enforcement-directorate to t=min:ministry-of-finance with pred analytic is a sensible pairing.
verdicts.baseRate: I checked the arithmetic and it holds. 70.86/18.40 = 3.851, and 3.851^(1/9) gives 16.2% a year. 550.75/81.01 = 6.798, and 6.798^(1/11) gives 19.0% a year. What the claim lacks is a denominator. Union total expenditure BE grew from ₹4,77,829 cr (2004-05) to ₹16,65,297 cr (2013-14, Budget at a Glance), about 14.9% a year. The 2004-05 Budget at a Glance prints total receipts BE as ₹5,37,829 cr; on that base the rate is about 13.4%. In the NDA window it grew from ₹17,94,892 cr (BE 2014-15) to about ₹50,65,345 cr (BE 2025-26), about 9.9% a year. So against the Union budget, the ED line ran only 1–3 points ahead under UPA but about 9 points ahead under NDA. Both rates are nominal, and CPI inflation was higher in 2004–14 (about 7–8%) than in 2014–25 (about 5%), so in real terms the gap is wider than 16.2 against 19.0 suggests. The UPA rate also depends heavily on the endpoints. UPA-II alone (BE 2009-10 ₹51.42 cr to BE 2013-14 ₹70.86 cr) gives about 8.3% a year, because BE 2009-10 was well above its actual (₹35.34 cr). BE 2008-09 ₹27.45 cr to BE 2013-14 gives about 20.9%. The SPEC control (UPA-II beside NDA on the same line) is run in symmetryCheck: actuals show 14.4% against 21.5%.
verdicts.denialFound: Not applicable. The claim is an analytic comparison of published budget lines and accuses no one, so no response was sought and none was needed. The ED's own Annual Report 2024-25 (PIB-hosted, https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2025/may/doc202551549501.pdf) gives context: 'In 2011, a comprehensive restructuring of ED was carried out and the sanctioned strength was increased to 2063. Since 2011, there has been no increase in...' (sanctioned strength). That supports the claim's point that the cadre expansion happened under UPA-II.
verdicts.innocentReading: The ED's mandate grew in steps: the PMLA came into force in 2005, the cadre was restructured from 745 to 2,063 posts in 2011, and later came FEOA 2018 and PMLA amendments. Pay commissions also lifted pay-heavy lines: the 6th CPC in 2008-09 (which matches the BE 2008-09 to BE 2009-10 jump from 27.45 to 51.42) and the 7th CPC in 2016. On small bases like these, nominal growth of 15–20% a year is what mandate growth plus pay revisions plus inflation would produce, under either government. The reading that the ED was 'already growing fast' is reasonable in nominal rupees. It is weaker once the line is set against the Union budget's own growth.
verdicts.reason: Every figure is confirmed in the primary PDFs, quoted as printed. EB 2004-05 Demand 42: '4. Enforcement Directorate 2047 ... 18.40 18.40' under 'Budget 2004-2005'. EB 2013-14 Demand 42: '5. Enforcement Directorate 2047 ... 70.86' under 'Budget 2013-2014', repeated in EB 2014-15, which also prints BE 2014-15 81.01. EB 2025-26 Demand 35: '3. Enforcement Directorate ... 550.75' under 'Budget 2025-2026', repeated in EB 2026-27. The 16.2% and 19.0% rates check out. The claim is correctly tiered analytic and carries an innocent reading. It survives as arithmetic. Its weak point is framing: it gives no denominator, which the contract requires ('Every figure beside its denominator and its comparison set'). Against Union total expenditure, ED growth was roughly in step with the budget under UPA but about twice the budget's pace under NDA. So 'continuation of a trend, not a break' (in the d field) is only half-supported. The fix is a correction, not a kill.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Write 'nominal' in the text: '16.2% a year in nominal terms … against 19.0%'. 2) Add the denominator: Union total expenditure BE grew about 14.9% a year from BE 2004-05 to BE 2013-14 (₹4,77,829 cr to ₹16,65,297 cr) and about 9.9% a year from BE 2014-15 to BE 2025-26 (₹17,94,892 cr to about ₹50,65,345 cr). The ED line ran 1.3 points ahead of the total under UPA and about 9 points ahead under NDA. 3) Soften the d-field sentence 'a continuation of an earlier trend, not a break from nothing' to: 'NDA-era nominal growth continued an earlier upward trend, but relative to total Union expenditure the gap widened from about 1 point to about 9 points a year.' 4) In d, change 'over nine budgets' to 'over nine years (ten budgets)' and 'over eleven budgets' to 'over eleven years (twelve budgets)'. 5) Add the endpoint caveat to innocentReading: UPA-II alone, BE 2009-10 to BE 2013-14, is 8.3% a year, because BE 2009-10 (₹51.42 cr) overshot its actual (₹35.34 cr). The BE 2008-09 to BE 2009-10 jump coincides with the 6th CPC. 6) Optional: give the BE 2026-27 endpoint as well. BE 2014-15 to BE 2026-27 (₹594.97 cr) is 18.1% a year, so the 19.0% figure depends on stopping at 2025-26. 7) Add the Budget at a Glance PDFs to srcs: ub2004-05/bag/bag2.pdf, ub2013-14/bag/bag2.pdf, ub2014-15/bag/bag2.pdf, budget2025-26/doc/Budget_at_Glance/bag2.pdf.

verdicts.dateTest: Restated as: the Union (MHA, Demand 54/55/48/51 Police) spent X on major head 4055 across the seven CAPF lines, FY2010-11 to FY2024-25 actuals. The windows are UPA-II FY2010-11 to FY2013-14 and NDA FY2014-15 to FY2024-25, and they meet cleanly at 1 April 2014. FY2014-15 was budgeted by UPA-II in the Feb 2014 interim budget and by NDA in the July 2014 full budget, so it belongs to NDA as spent. The comparison leaves out FY2009-10, which the SPEC places in UPA-II, because the 2009-10 actuals in the file have no Assam Rifles split. Without Assam Rifles, FY2009-10 is 2.81%, so leaving it out does not flatter either side. The real date problem is the trend inside each window. Recomputed from the file's actual rows, the share runs 2010-11 3.30%, 2011-12 3.23%, 2012-13 2.42%, 2013-14 1.85%, 2014-15 1.64%, 2015-16 1.65%, 2016-17 1.81%, 2017-18 2.08%, 2018-19 1.72%, 2019-20 1.73%, 2020-21 1.16%, 2021-22 1.17%, 2022-23 1.47%, 2023-24 2.03%, 2024-25 1.88%. The decline starts in FY2012-13 under UPA-II, and UPA-II's last year (1.85%) is above the NDA average. The 2.61% UPA-II figure is carried by FY2010-11 and FY2011-12.
verdicts.identityTest: The seven lines are CRPF, NSG, BSF, ITBP, CISF, Assam Rifles and SSB, each split into 2055 (revenue) and 4055 (capital), as printed in each year's Notes on Demands. They are the same forces in every year. The Departmental Accounting Organisation and NATGRID lines are correctly left out. CISF is taken net of recoveries in both periods: the 2013-14 table is headed 'allocations, net of recoveries', and the 2026-27 table prints CISF 2024-25 as 15326.37 less 690.66, net 14635.71, which is the figure the file uses. The demand number changes over the years (54, 55, 48, 51) and the rows record it correctly in `head`.
verdicts.baseRate: Capital as a share of large manpower establishment lines falls almost everywhere when pay is revised. The 7th CPC took effect in FY2016-17, DA rises every year, and revenue on these lines grew about 4.6x (22,347 to 102,690 crore) while force-line capital grew about 2.6x (763 to 1,963 crore). A falling share is therefore what a denominator effect looks like and does not pick out any particular government. No CAPF-by-CAPF or state comparator was run, and only two periods exist, so no fraction can be computed. The same lens applied to UPA-II alone (FY2010-11 against FY2013-14) gives the same reading, a fall of 3.30% to 1.85%. The symmetry control therefore weakens the period contrast.
verdicts.denialFound: none found — not asked. The claim is an analytic computation that names no wrongdoing, and no MHA statement on the force-line capital share was located.
verdicts.innocentReading: The fall is mostly the denominator. Pay commissions, DA and new battalions inflate revenue while capital in the force lines stays at a few hundred crore per force. The force lines also hold only a narrow slice of CAPF capital, and that is true in both periods, not just under NDA. In 2011-12 actuals, CPO housing (item 29.01, 607.15 cr) and CPO buildings (item 30.01, 1,760.17 cr) sat in separate lines, as did Border Management capital (992.46 cr) and the aircraft/boats 'Misc. Items' line. In 2024-25, 'Building Projects of CAPFs and CPOs' was 1,894.58 cr, Border Infrastructure capital outlay 3,649.79 cr, BSF Air Wing 72.52 cr and Modernization Plan IV 119.24 cr. All of these lie outside the seven lines. Which way the ratio moves depends on which lines are counted: adding border infrastructure (BOPs and fencing, largely CAPF-used) probably raises the NDA figure, while adding CPO buildings probably lowers it.
verdicts.reason: The claim survives Lens A. The arithmetic reproduces exactly from the file's budget rows: UPA-II capital 3,048.04 of 116,729.12 crore and NDA 12,996.79 of 780,080.29 crore, giving 2.61% and 1.67%, with ratios of 37:1 and 59:1. I checked the rows against the primary PDFs I opened. The 2013-14 Demand 55 shows 2011-12 4055 actuals CRPF 325.09, NSG 36.51, BSF 263.47, ITBP 85.31, CISF 22.00, AR 96.60, SSB 55.57, which sum to 884.55. The 2026-27 Demand 51 shows 2024-25 capital CRPF 545.52, NSG 27.89, BSF 664.96, ITBP 133.31, CISF 54.03, AR 356.88, SSB 180.70. The 2016-17 Demand 48 shows CRPF 2014-15 4055 at 226.63. The 2026-27 scheme figures quoted in the innocentReading are also correct: Building Projects 5,040.87 and MP-IV 343.66 at BE 2026-27. The claim is analytic, implies no wrongdoing, and carries an innocentReading, so 'analytic' is the right tier. Lens B does not kill it, but it is misleading by how the periods are split. The series shows a decline that begins inside UPA-II (3.30% to 1.85% by FY2013-14), not a break in 2014. The innocentReading also does not say that the building and border lines were separate in both periods, or that border infrastructure capital, used largely by CAPFs, grew sharply under NDA. sourceCheck is 'partially' because the claim cites only 4 of the roughly 15 Expenditure Budget files its 15 years of actuals come from. The 2013-14 file supplies only 2011-12 actuals, and the 2018-19 file supplies only 2016-17.
verdicts.corrections: 1) In `d`, add the year-by-year series, or at least 'share already fell from 3.30% (FY2010-11) to 1.85% (FY2013-14) within UPA-II; NDA range 1.16%–2.08%'. Do not present the two period means alone. 2) Replace the innocentReading's 'so the force lines understate capital spending for both governments' with an explicit statement that building capital was in separate lines in both periods: FY2011-12 actuals, CPO residential accommodation 607.15 and CPO buildings 1,760.17 (items 29.01 and 30.01, Demand 55, EB 2013-14); FY2024-25 actuals, Building Projects of CAPFs and CPOs 1,894.58 (item 14.01, Demand 51, EB 2026-27). Also name Border Infrastructure capital outlay (FY2011-12 Border Management 992.46; FY2024-25 3,649.79) and MP-IV (separate from about FY2022-23; FY2024-25 actual 119.24) as excluded lines whose inclusion could move the comparison either way. 3) Add a phrase on the pay-revision denominator (7th CPC from FY2016-17). 4) In `srcs`, cite every Expenditure Budget Police demand file from which a t-2 actual was taken (EB 2012-13 sbe54 through EB 2026-27 sbe51), or point to the budgets rows. The 2013-14 file covers only FY2011-12. 5) Use the claim `text` field's name for the SSB ('Sashastra'/'Shashastra' is spelled both ways in the documents) consistently; this is cosmetic. 6) Add a `killIf`: 'reclassification of CAPF procurement between force lines and scheme lines (MP-III/MP-IV) shown to account for the gap'.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads: Union Budget (MHA Demand 51; MoD Demands 20, 21 and 22) allocates the figures stated at Budget Estimate stage for FY 2026-27 (1 Apr 2026 to 31 Mar 2027). All four Notes on Demands for Grants are the 2026-27 edition, and every figure comes from the 'Budget 2026-2027' column. The claim's from/to dates match the fiscal year. The killIf names supplementary demands. I found no 2026-27 supplementary batch that changes Defence Demands 20 or 21 materially (the ₹41,430 cr defence supplementary found was for FY 2025-26), so the BE ratio still stands as a BE figure. Pass.
verdicts.identityTest: Every entity and line matches the source. sbe51.pdf 'Establishment Expenditure of the Centre, 1. Central Armed Police Forces' lists items 1.01 to 1.07 (CRPF, NSG, BSF, ITBP, CISF net, Assam Rifles, SSB) plus 1.08 Departmental Accounting. 'Total- Central Armed Police Forces' is 114484.09 revenue, 2305.21 capital, 116789.30 total. Less 1.08 (202.14 total, 2.49 capital) this gives ₹116,587.16 cr, with capital ₹2,302.72 cr (1.975%, so 2.0%). sbe20 Net BE 2026-27 is ₹365,478.98 cr. sbe21 Net is ₹219,306.47 cr. The sum is ₹584,785.45 cr, of which capital is 37.50%. CAPF lines are 19.94% of that total. sbe22 Net is ₹171,338.22 cr. sbe20 item 1.01 'Pay and Allowances of the Army' is ₹118,167.91 cr. In PRS Table 4 ('Vacancies across CAPFs, as on January 2024', BPR&D 2024), the six forces CISF, CRPF, ITBP, SSB, AR and BSF sum to 10,26,879 sanctioned posts, which is about 10.3 lakh. The claim correctly says six forces, because NSG is not in the table. Caveat: the same PRS page also says 'As of July 2024, the total sanctioned strength of CAPFs was about 10.5 lakh personnel'. CISF is net of ₹855 cr recoveries, and Defence revenue is net of ₹7,060.71 cr receipts, so net is used consistently on both sides. Nothing in the claim joins individually true facts to imply something the sources do not say: it is a ratio of published lines.
verdicts.baseRate: This property does not single out one year or one government. The capital share of the same Demand 51 CAPF lines is 1.88% (Actuals 2024-25: 1966.14/104824.10), 1.77% (BE 2025-26) and 1.89% (RE 2025-26), and PRS says 2% capital 'is similar to the trends from last few years'. Every CAPF line except NSG (8.5%) and Assam Rifles (3.9%) sits under 2.5% capital. The claim alleges nothing, so the SPEC control (UPA-II beside NDA on the same line) would change no reading. It was not run, though, and the symmetryCheck should carry the UPA-II CAPF capital share for completeness.
verdicts.denialFound: Not applicable. The claim is an analytic budget comparison that accuses no party. None found; not asked.
verdicts.innocentReading: CAPFs are manpower-heavy police forces under MHA, and Defence Services carries platform acquisition. Part of the gap is also how the budget is booked. Much CAPF capital sits outside the seven establishment lines in Demand 51: item 14.01 'Building Projects of CAPFs and Central Police Organisations' (₹5,040.87 cr capital, shared with IB and the CPOs), item 16 'Modernization Plan IV for CAPFs' (₹252.18 cr capital) and item 12 'BSF Air Wing, Aircrafts, River Boats and Helibase' (₹72.01 cr capital). Defence Demand 21 includes works and buildings. Counting Mod Plan IV and BSF Air Wing raises the CAPF capital share only to about 2.2%. Adding all of 14.01 takes it to about 6.3%, which is still far below 37.5%. So the comparison holds in direction, but the 2.0% versus 37.5% contrast is not like-for-like on works capital.
verdicts.reason: Every number in the claim matches the primary 2026-27 Notes on Demands for Grants (sbe51, sbe20, sbe21, sbe22) and PRS Table 4 to the paisa, and the arithmetic reproduces exactly: 116,587.16, 2,302.72 (2.0%), 584,785.45 (37.5%) and 19.9%. The claim is our own ratio, carries an innocentReading, alleges nothing, and names no person, deployment or unpublished budget. Analytic is the correct tier. The only weakness is scope: the 'capital share' comparison leaves out CAPF capital booked elsewhere in Demand 51, while Defence capital includes works. That calls for a scoping note, not a kill, because the share stays far below the Defence share however the extra lines are counted.
verdicts.corrections: 1. In `d`, add a scope sentence: "CAPF capital outside these lines in Demand 51, BE 2026-27: item 16 Modernization Plan IV for CAPFs ₹252.18 cr capital; item 12 BSF Air Wing ₹72.01 cr capital; item 14.01 Building Projects of CAPFs and CPOs ₹5,040.87 cr (shared with IB/CPOs, not split by force). Including 12 and 16 gives about 2.2%; including all of 14.01 gives about 6.3%. Defence Demand 21 includes works capital." 2. Note that CISF 1.05 is net of ₹855 cr recoveries (gross ₹16,828.85 cr), so CAPF lines gross are about ₹117,442 cr. 3. For strength, cite '10,26,879 sanctioned (sum of PRS Table 4, Jan 2024, six forces excl. NSG)' and record that the PRS text gives 'about 10.5 lakh as of July 2024'. 4. Revise innocentReading so the low capital share is attributed partly to booking CAPF buildings and modernisation in separate Demand 51 scheme lines. 5. Add a symmetryCheck row with the CAPF-line capital share for a UPA-II year (e.g. BE 2013-14) beside BE 2026-27. 6. Optionally replace upgradeIf with something testable, e.g. 'Demand 51 restructures CAPF capital into the establishment lines'.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim restated: "the CAPFs (six forces, per BPR&D via PRS) had 1,026,879 sanctioned and 952,764 actual personnel as on 1 January 2024, which is 73.3 and 68.0 per lakh of projected population; State and UT police had 155 actual per lakh at the same date; the CAPF vacancy rate was 14% on 1.1.2012, 6% on 1.1.2014, 15% on 1.1.2017 and 7.2% on 1.1.2024." No actor tenure is involved, and every figure is dated to the reference date its source prints. PRS 2018-19 Table 3 says "Figures for each year are as of January 1 of that year": 2012 8.9/7.6/14%, 2013 9%, 2014 6%, 2015 7%, 2016 7%, 2017 10.8/9.2/15%. PRS 2026-27 Table 4 is headed "Vacancies across CAPFs, as on January 2024". The 155 figure is from the same date: PRS says "As of January 2024, India has 155 police personnel for every one lakh people." The PIB figure of 8.0% is dated 01.07.2024 and is correctly kept separate from January.
verdicts.identityTest: The entity matches, but two series are spliced together. PRS 2026-27 Table 4 lists six forces (CISF, CRPF, ITBP, SSB, AR, BSF); NSG is not in it, and the record says so. PRS 2018-19 Table 3 covers "the seven central armed police forces" (NSG included). So the 2012-17 vacancy points (seven forces) and the 7.2% for 2024 (six forces) are not strictly like-for-like. NSG is small (about 1% of posts), so the distortion is minor, but the text should state it. The 155 figure is the All-India actual from PRS Table 22 ("All India | 197 | 155"). It is State/UT police, which is the right comparison family. However, it is an actual figure, while the claim text sets the CAPF sanctioned figure (73.3) beside it as well. The like-for-like pairs are 68.0 vs 155 (actual) and 73.3 vs 197 (sanctioned). The denominator also differs. CAPF per-lakh uses NCP 2020 projections interpolated to 2024. I checked MoSPI Table 1.1: 2021 = 1363.00 mn and 2026 = 1425.90 mn, which gives 1400.74 mn = 14,007.4 lakh, so it is confirmed. BPR&D's 155 uses BPR&D's own population base, which is not published in the source.
verdicts.baseRate: Persistent CAPF vacancy is not specific to any government. It was 14% and 9% under UPA-II (Jan 2012, 2013) and between 6% and 15% under NDA (2014-2024). PRS says "At least 8% of CAPF posts have been vacant in the last six years." Applying the same lens to the SPEC's UPA-II/NDA control gives no partisan reading, and the claim asserts none. The CAPF-vs-state per-lakh comparison has no comparable family because there is one central pool. State per-lakh varies very widely (Bihar 80 to Nagaland 1,124 per PRS), so 155 is an all-India mean and not a norm.
verdicts.denialFound: No denial is needed because the claim alleges no wrongdoing. The MHA's own framing is in the same PIB release (24 JUL 2024, https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2036391): "number of vacancies as on 01.07.2024 in the Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) and Assam Rifles(AR) are 84,106 against total sanctioned strength of 10,45,751. Filling up of vacancies is a continuous process..." PRS also records the government's remedy: a 10% reservation for ex-Agniveers, plus age and physical-standard relaxations.
verdicts.innocentReading: The existing innocentReading fits. CAPFs are a deployable central reserve, not population-proportional policing, so the per-lakh figure measures scale, not coverage. The 15% for 2017 is largely a denominator effect: sanctioned strength jumped from 9.7 to 10.8 lakh in a year while actual strength rose only from 9.0 to 9.2 lakh, so newly sanctioned posts not yet recruited show up as vacancies. Recruitment runs in UPSC/SSC cycles.
verdicts.reason: Every number checks against the sources I opened. PRS 2026-27 Table 4: the six force rows sum to sanctioned 1,026,879 and actual 952,764, so vacancy is 7.217%. Dividing both by 14,007.4 lakh gives 73.31 and 68.02 per lakh. PRS states 155 per lakh for January 2024. PRS 2018-19 Table 3 gives 14% (2012), 6% (2014) and 15% (2017). PIB gives 84,106 against 10,45,751. MoSPI's projections reproduce the denominator. The claim is our own derived comparison with no wrongdoing implied and an innocentReading present, so analytic is the correct tier. Nothing refutes it. The remaining defects are presentational: the 2012-17 seven-force series is spliced with the 2024 six-force figure; sanctioned CAPF strength is set beside actual State police strength; and the short text drops the 8.5-11.3% values for 2019-2023, so the arc "15% to 7.2%" reads as steadier improvement than the series shows.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Text: change "beside 155 per lakh for State and UT police" to "beside 155 actual (197 sanctioned) per lakh for State and UT police (BPR&D via PRS Table 22, January 2024; BPR&D population base differs from the NCP projection used for CAPFs)". 2) Text: make the vacancy trend "14% (2012), 6% (2014), 15% (2017; seven forces incl. NSG), 8.5-11.3% (2019-2021), 9.3% (2023), 7.2% (Jan 2024; six forces, NSG excluded); 8.0% on 1 July 2024 (PIB)", so the 2019-21 rise and the change in force coverage are visible. 3) d: add that the 2017 jump comes from sanctioned strength rising 9.7 to 10.8 lakh (new posts), not from attrition. 4) d: cite MoSPI Table 1.1 (2021 = 1363.00 mn, 2026 = 1425.90 mn; interpolated 2024 = 1400.74 mn) as the denominator source. 5) killIf can stay, but the PRS transcription is internally consistent: the row sums reproduce PRS's percentages.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: the Union (MHA) released 7–30% of ASUMP allocation to States, FY2020-21 to FY2024-25 (as on 27.03.2025). Source window is the LS USQ 4862 Annexure of 01.04.2025, columns 2020-21 to 2024-25 "(As on 27.03.2025)". from/to (2020-04-01 to 2025-03-27) match. FY2024-25 is a partial year (to 27.03.2025), so that year's 20.0% is provisional, and the record already says so through its 'to' date. The BE/RE 2022-23 figures (621.45 / 152.52) appear in the EB 2023-24 columns "Budget 2022-2023" and "Revised 2022-2023". The 2022-23 actual (34.72) is in EB 2024-25, column "Actual 2022-2023". Dates pass.
verdicts.identityTest: The actor is MHA, the scheme is ASUMP, which the answer calls "[erstwhile scheme of 'Modernization of State Police Forces (MPF)']". That matches force:mpf-scheme. "28 States" means the 29 rows of Table I minus J&K, which is shown as "-" or "***" and moved to the UT table (Table II) from 2022-23. One caveat: the EB line is "Modernisation of State Police Forces and Crime and Criminal Tracking Network and Systems (CCTNS)", item 28.01 in EB 2023-24 and 27.01 in EB 2024-25. It is a wider line than ASUMP-to-States, so its 34.72 cannot be read as ASUMP alone. Table I and Table II releases for 2022-23 add to 31.06 + 5.447 = 36.51, which does not equal 34.72. That is a different accounting basis, not a contradiction, but the claim should not imply the two are the same quantity.
verdicts.baseRate: Recomputed from all 28 State rows. Zero-release States per year: 16, 13, 0, 18, 13. Release share of allocation: 19.8, 30.4, 7.1, 19.0, 20.0%. The column sums reproduce the printed totals (103.02, 158.39, 31.0621, 45.1785, 96.61). Nil in at least 3 of 5 years: 12 States (AR, BR, HR, JH, KL, MH, ML, MN, MZ, PB, TN, WB). Nil in 4 years: AR, JH, MH, MN, TN. All of this matches the record exactly. Release below allocation is near-universal: in FY2022-23 all 28 States got less than allocation, and in most years more than 80% did. The property is therefore not specific to West Bengal. The 12-State group mixes BJP/NDA-run States (Arunachal, Haryana, Manipur, Bihar, Maharashtra after mid-2022, Meghalaya under an NDA ally) with opposition-run ones (WB, TN, Kerala, Jharkhand, Punjab). It does not separate by party, and the claim says plainly that no ruling-party split was run. The UPA-II control was not run on this line.
verdicts.denialFound: The MHA's own answer gives the reason (LS USQ 4862, https://www.mha.gov.in/MHA1/Par2017/pdfs/par2025-pdfs/LS01042025/4862.pdf): "Where release is less than allocation, the same is on account of non-submission of Utilization Certificates (UCs)". On West Bengal it adds: "had high unspent balances (central share) of around of Rs. 69 cr. as on 01.04.2022, Rs. 39 cr. as on 03.04.2023 and Rs. 11 cr. as on 05.04.2024. Accordingly, the State was not eligible for release". The BJP's Amit Malviya (https://x.com/amitmalviya/status/1953071100142989412) blames the WB government. I found no response from the West Bengal government on ASUMP releases. It was not asked by this file.
verdicts.innocentReading: The Department of Expenditure's release guidelines for centrally sponsored schemes bar a further tranche while unspent balances and utilisation certificates are pending. Most States carry such balances, so releases sit far below allocation everywhere. FY2022-23 was low because ASUMP guidelines were only circulated on 08.08.2022, after the Cabinet extended the scheme on 19.01.2022 (Table II note), and every State got only a token ₹0.33–4.8 cr. From FY2024-25 the SNA-SPARSH fund-flow model added another gate. The pattern is the Union's rules meeting State accounting. It shows no partisan targeting, and the claim asserts none.
verdicts.reason: Every State-level figure, ratio and count reproduces exactly from the Parliament answer's Annexure, which I opened and recomputed: 7.1–30.4%, 12 of 28 States, West Bengal nil in 3 of 5 years, 5 States nil in 4. BE 621.45 and RE 152.52 for 2022-23 are confirmed in EB 2023-24, item 28.01. The claim is our own counting with an innocent reading attached and an explicit statement that no ruling-party split was run, so the analytic tier is correct and implies no wrongdoing. Two problems remain, both in the source chain rather than the substance. First, the actual of ₹34.72 cr is not in any cited source. It is printed only in EB 2024-25 (https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/budget2024-25/doc/eb/sbe51.pdf, item 27.01, "Actual 2022-2023": 34.72), which the budgets row cites but the claim does not. Second, the cited EB 2026-27 carries 2024-25 to 2026-27 figures and supports none of the claim's numbers.
verdicts.corrections: 1. Replace the src "Expenditure Budget 2026-27, Demand 51" (https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/doc/eb/sbe51.pdf) with "Expenditure Budget 2024-25, Demand 51 (Police), item 27.01, Actual 2022-23" (https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/budget2024-25/doc/eb/sbe51.pdf), which is the source of the 34.72 figure. Keep EB 2023-24 (item 28.01) for BE 621.45 and RE 152.52. 2. In d/text, rename the EB line in full as "Modernisation of State Police Forces and CCTNS (includes CCTNS; not ASUMP-to-States alone)". Note that ASUMP releases for 2022-23 to States plus UTs (Tables I and II) were ₹36.51 cr, against an EB actual of ₹34.72 cr on a different accounting basis. 3. Add the context for FY2022-23 from the Table II note: ASUMP guidelines were circulated only on 08.08.2022, and every State got a token release that year. 4. In text, write "7.1–30.4%" rather than "7-30%", and note that FY2024-25 is as on 27.03.2025. 5. Record that the UPA-II and party-split controls were not run on this line, and that no West Bengal government response was found.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim, written out: the Ministry of Finance (MoS Pankaj Chaudhary) reported in Parliament that PMLA Special Courts gave 56 judgments on merits with 53 convictions, from 01.04.2014 to 30.11.2025. The answer is LS USQ 1310 of 08.12.2025. Its ECIR count (6,444) and prosecution-complaint count (1,843+573=2,416) cover the same window, "Since 2014-15" to "till November, 2025". The windows overlap, so the date test passes. The ED Annual Report 2024-25 (PIB-hosted, May 2025) counts "47 cases decided till date", which is all-time and not limited to 2014 onward. That is a different window from the Lok Sabha answer. The record's "(as at its date)" is accurate but should say the count is all-time. A later Rajya Sabha answer (04.08.2026, to V. Sivadasan, as reported by The Wire and the420.in) updates the series to 2026 dates. It does not revise the 30.11.2025 figures, so the killIf is not triggered.
verdicts.identityTest: The actors are right. The Directorate of Enforcement (Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance) is the agency, and the statute is PMLA 2002. Both sources name ED/PMLA. Annexure III of USQ 1310 is headed "Enforcement Directorate". No person below public rank is named. The minister is named only as the answering office.
verdicts.baseRate: The property in question is a gap between a merits-only rate and a pipeline rate. The gap is not discriminating, because every Indian prosecuting agency's merits-decided rate is far above convictions per case registered. For example, the ITD in the same answer has 522 convictions against 13,877 prosecutions filed. The identical lens gives an even lower pipeline figure for the UPA-era base: 1,883 ECIRs before April 2014, and the AR's year-wise conviction chart starts at 0. So the lens does not separate governments. The claim does not attribute the gap to one government, which is correct.
verdicts.denialFound: The ED's own response is embedded in a source and quoted accurately. The ED Annual Report 2024-25, p.107, says: "It is pertinent to note that the conviction rate is a measure of outcomes in disposed cases, and not a ratio of convictions to total number of ongoing investigations or pending trials." It also blames delay on "the general delay in judicial system ... procedural linkages with the trial of the predicate offence" (https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2025/may/doc202551549501.pdf). In RS answer 04.08.2026, the government also said that convictions "may pertain to cases filed in different years" (reported at https://m.thewire.in/article/law/cases-under-pmla-by-enforcement-directorate-rose-to-four-year-high-in-2025-26-parliament-told/amp).
verdicts.innocentReading: Both ratios are correct arithmetic: 53/56=94.64%, 53/6,444=0.82%, 53/2,416=2.19%. They answer different questions. Most PMLA complaints (1,739 per the AR) are still in trial, and those trials usually wait for the predicate offence. Convictions in 2014-25 may also come from pre-2014 ECIRs, so the pipeline ratio mixes cohorts. Neither ratio shows that any investigation was ill-founded or politically targeted. The record's innocentReading already says this.
verdicts.reason: I opened both sources and every number matches the printed text. USQ 1310 Annexure I: ECIRs total 6,444. Annexure III: "1843+573=2416"; "judgments on merits on the issue of Money-Laundering in 56 instances, out of which conviction orders have been passed in 53 instances convicting 121 accused ... 53/56*100=94.64%". ED AR 2024-25: "Till date, ED has filed PCs in 1,739 cases, which are presently at various stages of trial"; "Of the 47 cases decided till date, only 3 have resulted in acquittals on merit"; "convictions in 44 cases, leading to the conviction of 100 persons"; and the quoted "measure of outcomes in disposed cases" sentence. The claim is our own two-denominator comparison, carries an innocentReading and implies no wrongdoing, so analytic is the right tier. Three framing points weaken it but do not refute it: the "of" wording implies the 53 are a subset of the 6,444; the 2,416 denominator counts supplementary complaints as if they were cases; and "cases decided" should read "instances". The fixes are below.
verdicts.corrections: (1) Text: "53 of 6,444 ECIRs (0.8%)" implies the 53 convictions arise from those 6,444 ECIRs. The government says convictions and filings "are not directly correlated", and some convictions may come from the 1,883 pre-April-2014 ECIRs. Reword as "53 convictions against 6,444 ECIRs recorded in the same window (0.8%)" and add "cohorts not matched" to d. (2) Text: "2.2% of prosecution complaints filed" misdescribes the denominator. 2,416 is 1,843 prosecution complaints plus 573 supplementary complaints, and supplementary complaints are filed in existing cases. Write "2.2% of PCs plus supplementary PCs (2.9% of the 1,843 main PCs)". (3) Replace "56 cases decided on merits" with "56 instances of judgments on merits on the money-laundering issue", as the answer prints it. This count excludes discharges and other non-merits disposals. (4) In d, mark the AR's 47/44/3 as all-time ("till date", c. April 2025), not from 01.04.2014. (5) Add as a later data point, not a supersession: RS answer of 04.08.2026 (MoS Pankaj Chaudhary to V. Sivadasan), with FY2025-26 ECIRs of 1,080 and updated conviction counts. Press reports differ on the conviction figure: one summary gives 56 convictions and 124 accused (93.33%) as of 31.03.2026, while The Wire says 43 cases and 104 persons. Verify the RS PDF before adding any figure. The killIf is not triggered because the 30.11.2025 figures were not revised. (6) Add to symmetryCheck: applied to the UPA-era base (1,883 ECIRs before April 2014, near-zero convictions), the identical pipeline lens gives the same or a lower ratio, so the lens is not partisan.
